Although the sRGB image is widely adopted in existing auto-exposure algorithms, exposure times of blocks in the highlight and shadow regions might not be accurately learned due to the limited radiance measurement capability of the sRGB image. This paper thus also explores the feasibility of temporary image as a raw image. Due to the better radiance measurement capability of the raw image, the exposure times of blocks are learned more accurately, and more details in the highlight/shadow regions of the real-world HDR scene are captured by the resultant HDR imaging system. Experiment results validate the proposed neural block-wise auto-exposure algorithm.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: VideoHarness-SRSI: Structured Recursive Self-Improvement for Video Understanding Harness
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: LLM system capabilities depend not only on model parameters but also on the executable harnesses that organize information acquisition, tool use, reasoning, and memory. Recursive harness evolution can automate their design, but how it can reliably discover generalizable systems from limited, noisy, and repeatedly reused feedback remains unclear. We study this question in agentic video understanding, where rich multimodal evidence and coupled mechanisms make harness optimization challenging. We first introduce VHarness-BRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework that evolves video harnesses around a frozen vision-language model. Analyzing over 4,000 evolved candidates, we find it competitive with hand-engineered systems but identify three interconnected failure modes: validation overfitting, search-budget dilution, and the early-experience trap. We trace all three to a common root: the same imperfect validation evidence drives both harness revisions and the proposer's search strategy. We therefore propose VHarness-SRSI, an evidence-governed framework in which every search decision rests on evidence that is transferable, sufficient, and gathered before the search commits. It restricts the proposer to content-free feedback, informs exploration with instrumented warm-up experiments, and develops mechanisms in isolated probe-race branches before factorial composition and joint refinement. Across four video understanding benchmarks, VideoHarness-SRSI improves the equally weighted mean held-out score by 6.2% relative to VideoHarness-BRSI and reduces the mean validation-test gap by 37.9%. Reliable harness evolution thus depends on how search is organized and informed, not only on how well it optimizes validation performance.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Dusting the Phantom: Gaussian Allocation for Fading Dynamic Content
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Dynamic Gaussian representations have made high-quality, real-time volumetric video increasingly practical, yet challenging motion can still break their reconstruction: small fast-moving objects may disappear, and fine textures in highly dynamic regions are often lost. In particular, simply training longer or using more Gaussians may still fail to recover small, fast-moving objects. We argue that the key bottleneck is not representational capacity itself, but where and when Gaussian primitives are allocated. Existing allocation strategies rely on current Gaussian locations and often overlook the spatiotemporal destinations of relocated Gaussians. To address these limitations, we introduce two complementary strategies. First, Seed Injection identifies under-reconstructed dynamic regions using temporal appearance changes and reconstruction errors, and initializes new Gaussians at geometrically plausible 3D locations through multi-view observations, independent of existing Gaussian locations. Second, Temporal Biased Relocation uses time-resolved optimization signals to guide the spatiotemporal placement of relocated Gaussians. Both strategies maintain a fixed Gaussian budget without modifying the underlying representation. Experiments across multiple dynamic-scene datasets demonstrate improved reconstruction quality, particularly in highly dynamic regions, recovering small, rapidly moving objects and fine-grained appearance details.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: ManiFusion: Unlocking the High-Throughput Generation via Superposition in Manifold Space
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Diffusion models achieve high-quality image generation but remain computationally expensive due to iterative denoising across many timesteps. Existing acceleration methods mainly reduce per-sample latency, but gains along this axis are becoming saturated. We instead explore an orthogonal throughput-oriented direction by processing multiple samples within a single denoising evaluation. To this end, we propose ManiFusion, a backbone-agnostic framework for multi-sample generation through fused-space computation. ManiFusion jointly processes multiple samples by fusing them before the denoising backbone and separating them afterward through unfusion. We provide a geometric perspective on how multiple samples can share a fused representation while retaining the information needed to guide their individual generation trajectories. To better align fusion allocation with denoising stages, ManiFusion uses Trajectory-Fusion Scheduling (TFS), which dynamically adjusts fusion factors throughout sampling. ManiFusion generalizes across diffusion families, including both U-Net and transformer backbones in pixel and latent spaces. We further show that ManiFusion composes with existing acceleration methods and reaches throughput regimes unattainable by prior approaches with minimal quality degradation.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Beyond Generation: Using Multimodal LLMs as Detectors of LLM-Generated Deepfake Facial Images
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: As image generation models become increasingly capable of producing highly realistic content, traditional forensic techniques are struggling to keep up. This paper investigates whether MLLMs can instead be used as a form of forensic analysis by identifying synthetic media. Specifically, the study aims to determine whether these models detect fake images by recognising physical inconsistencies, or whether they rely on digital artefacts such as embedded watermarks. Six MLLMs (GPT-4o, GPT-5, GPT-5.2, Gemini 2.5, Gemini 3, and Seed 1.6) are benchmarked using a dataset of 400 images. Fifty images are authentic photographs, while the remaining 350 are generated using seven leading image models: Gemini 3, Gemini 2.5, Flux.2 Pro, GPT-Image-1, GPT-Image-1.5, Seedream 4.0, and Seedream 4.5. The evaluation is structured in three stages: single-image classification, pairwise comparison, and a focused "self-detection" experiment on Gemini. Several MLLMs achieved a high detection accuracy, with GPT-5.2 reaching a peak of 97.9% in the pairwise experiment, against specific generators and an overall mean pairwise accuracy of 82.5% by identifying structural or physical inconsistencies within images. However, results from the self-detection experiment indicate that the presence of invisible SynthID watermarks leads to a 10% reduction in Gemini's detection accuracy compared to the clean control group. One possible explanation is that SynthID embedding reduces some of the visible artefacts the models rely on for detection. These results imply that MLLMs can detect structural artefacts without relying on watermarks, but performance varies substantially across model generations. The findings also suggest that SynthID embedding may suppress some of the structural artefacts used during detection.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: FALCON: FPGA-Accelerated Latency-Certifiable Occupancy Networks for Camera-Based Autonomous Driving
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: A perception system that must brake for a pedestrian does not need a low average latency. It must deliver an answer before the deadline on every frame, the worst case included. Commodity edge accelerators optimize the mean through dynamic scheduling, OS jitter, thermal throttling, and contention, so their per-frame latency can be measured but not bounded. We build FALCON, a camera-based 3D occupancy front-end on the AMD Kria KR260, an embedded FPGA drawing 4.3 W idle and up to 6.6 W under inference, and make the latency guarantee layered and explicit: programmable-logic (PL) compute is cycle-bounded analytically; inference is a measured envelope over 100k-frame traces; and a watchdog enforces output delivery, publishing the previous output flagged stale when a frame is late. The deadline runs use a fixed-work proxy of six ResNet-50 DPU inferences per frame, not the full occupancy network: across three 100k-frame enforced runs, all 300k proxy frames delivered an output within the 100 ms deadline plus at most 10.2 ms, the worst of the three runs. The full six-camera FlashOcc pipeline composes to about 1.3 s per frame on the board and is not yet a 10 Hz system. The two operations the DPU cannot run, a view-transform gather and a bilinear resize, become fixed-trip-count PL IPs numerically matched to their software references. On the full Occ3D-nuScenes validation set the board reaches mIoU 29.88, 92.8% of an FP32 baseline the DPU cannot run. On a ResNet-50 probe over 100k frames the KR260 tail stays within 1.5 times its median (2.0 times for the six-inference proxy), where Jetson Orin reaches 4.4 times and the worst datacenter GPU run (NVIDIA L4) 23.6 times. The deployment recipe, HLS sources, and raw timing traces are released.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: WaveLLM: Wavelet-Domain LLM Entropy Modeling for Lossless Image Compression
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Lossless image compression fundamentally relies on accurate entropy modeling, driving a recent shift toward large language model (LLM)-based methods. However, existing approaches mainly emphasize the modeling capacity of LLMs while directly serializing images into pixel or residual sequences, leaving heterogeneous signal patterns entangled within a single prediction stream. In this paper, we argue that effective entropy modeling depends not only on model capacity, but also on the predictability of the input representation. Motivated by this insight, we propose WaveLLM, a wavelet-domain LLM-based entropy model for lossless image compression. By decomposing an image into multi-level wavelet subbands, WaveLLM converts a heterogeneous prediction problem into a set of more structured and statistically homogeneous subproblems that are more amenable to autoregressive probability estimation. To bridge numerical coding symbols with the LLM's native text token space, we introduce a dedicated numerical interface featuring value embeddings and a coefficient prediction head. Furthermore, a task-adaptive prompting strategy is designed to enable a single shared model to adapt to diverse subbands within a unified framework. Built on Llama-3.2-3B with LoRA adaptation, WaveLLM achieves 2.51, 2.24, and 2.27 bpsp on Kodak, CLIC Pro, and DIV2K, respectively, outperforming the PixelCNN-based codec using the same wavelet transform by 0.43, 0.36, and 0.46 bpsp, and surpassing recent LLM-based lossless compressors on all three benchmarks.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Beyond Boundaries: A Comprehensive Survey of Transferable Attacks on AI Systems
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Transferable attacks allow adversarial manipulations or learned attack mechanisms constructed in one setting to compromise other AI systems, potentially reducing attack costs and amplifying security and privacy risks. Yet fragmented terminology and evaluation practices hinder understanding of what transfers, why it transfers, and where transfer fails. This survey synthesizes representative research and develops a unified taxonomy spanning six complementary axes: cross-instance, cross-domain, cross-modality, cross-model, cross-task, and cross-deployment. By separating source-target configuration changes from attacker access and adaptation budgets, the taxonomy provides a common framework for comparing transfer across evasion, poisoning, backdoors, privacy inference, model stealing, and prompt-based attacks. We connect transfer mechanisms, including gradient alignment, shared representations, training persistence, and deployment invariances, to enhancement methods based on augmentation, disentanglement, and optimization. Our synthesis identifies inconsistent transfer, incompatible metrics, and gaps between simulated and physical evaluations, and establishes a research agenda for compositional transfer, configuration differences, temporal persistence, and reproducible benchmarking. Together, this work supports systematic investigation of shared vulnerabilities and guides transfer-aware security assessment and defense.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Harmful YouTube Video Detection: A Taxonomy of Online Harm and MLLMs as Alternative Annotators
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Video platforms, used by billions globally, are criticized for exposing users to harmful content. Yet, detecting online harm remains challenging due to inconsistent approaches to what constitutes harm and limitations of human annotation. We address both challenges. Theoretically, we integrate and expand existing taxonomies and platform guidelines to multimodal contexts and develop a comprehensive taxonomy for online harm. We categorize online harm on video platforms into six content-based categories: Information, Hate and harassment, Addictive, Clickbait, Sexual, and Physical harms. Methodologically, we propose and systematically test multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as alternative annotators of harmful videos. We curate a dataset of 19,422 potentially harmful YouTube videos and annotate them using GPT-4-Turbo, non-trained crowdworkers, and trained annotators. We discuss the potential applications of MLLMs in platform content moderation and social science research, particularly in contexts where they perform comparably to human annotators in binary and multi-label classification tasks.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Less is More: Efficient Black-box Attribution via Minimal Interpretable Subset Selection
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: To develop a trustworthy AI system, it is essential to understand its behavior using attribution methods, which aim to identify the input regions that most influence the model's decisions. For discrete inputs such as images, however, accurately identifying input-prediction interactions is particularly challenging because of combinatorial explosion. We formulate black-box attribution as an ordered interpretable subset-selection problem. Inspired by the marginal-gain principle of submodular optimization, the formulation permits redundancy, positive complementarity, and negative interference among input sub-regions. We propose LiMA (Less input is More faithful for Attribution), which ranks sub-regions by their contributions along a sequence of selected subsets. LiMA employs a composite objective that evaluates subsets through semantic consistency, collaboration, prediction confidence, and semantic effectiveness. We further design a bidirectional greedy search to efficiently identify important and non-critical sub-regions. Experiments on eight foundation models (CLIP, ImageBind, LanguageBind, QuiltNet, etc.) and six datasets (ImageNet, VGG-Sound, CUB-200-2011, etc.) demonstrate strong generalization and faithful interpretations with fewer sub-regions. LiMA achieves state-of-the-art Insertion, Deletion, and average highest confidence, with average improvements of 36.3% in Insertion and 39.6% in Deletion; it is also 1.6 times faster than naive greedy search. For failure attribution on incorrect predictions, LiMA improves average highest confidence by 86.1% over state-of-the-art methods. The code is available at https://github.com/RuoyuChen10/LIMA.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: FlexPainter: Flexible and Multi-View Consistent Texture Generation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Texture map production is an important part of 3D modeling and determines the rendering quality. Recently, diffusion-based methods have opened a new way for texture generation. However, restricted control flexibility and limited prompt modalities may prevent creators from producing desired results. Furthermore, inconsistencies between generated multi-view images often lead to poor texture generation quality. To address these issues, we introduce \textbf{FlexPainter}, a novel texture generation pipeline that enables flexible multi-modal conditional guidance and achieves highly consistent texture generation. A shared conditional embedding space is constructed to perform flexible aggregation between different input modalities. Utilizing such embedding space, we present an image-based CFG method to decompose structural and style information, achieving reference image-based stylization. Leveraging the 3D knowledge within the image diffusion prior, we first generate multi-view images simultaneously using a grid representation to enhance global understanding. Meanwhile, we propose a view synchronization and adaptive weighting module during diffusion sampling to further ensure local consistency. Finally, a 3D-aware texture completion model combined with a texture enhancement model is used to generate seamless, high-resolution texture maps. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that our framework significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both flexibility and generation quality.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Towards Unified World Models for Visual Navigation via Memory-Augmented Planning and Foresight
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Enabling embodied agents to imagine future states is essential for robust and generalizable visual navigation. Yet, state-of-the-art systems typically rely on modular designs that decouple navigation planning from visual world modeling, which often induces state-action misalignment and weak adaptability in novel or dynamic scenarios. We propose UniWM, a unified, memory-augmented world model that integrates egocentric visual foresight and planning within a single multimodal autoregressive backbone. UniWM explicitly grounds action selection in visually imagined outcomes, tightly aligning prediction with control. Meanwhile, a hierarchical memory mechanism fuses short-term perceptual cues with longer-term trajectory context, supporting stable and coherent reasoning over extended horizons. Extensive experiments on four challenging benchmarks (Go Stanford, ReCon, SCAND, HuRoN) and the 1X Humanoid Dataset show that UniWM improves navigation success rates by up to 30%, substantially reduces trajectory errors against strong baselines, generalizes zero-shot to the unseen TartanDrive dataset, and scales naturally to high-dimensional humanoid navigation. These results position UniWM as a principled step toward unified, imagination-driven embodied navigation. The code and models are available at https://github.com/UWMILab/UniWM.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: CoatFusion: Controllable Material Coating in Images
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: We introduce Material Coating, a novel image editing task that simulates applying a thin material layer onto an object while preserving its underlying coarse and fine geometry. Material coating is fundamentally different from existing "material transfer" methods, which are designed to replace an object's intrinsic material, often overwriting fine details. To address this new task, we construct a large-scale synthetic dataset (110K images) of 3D objects with varied, physically-based coatings, named DataCoat110K. We then propose CoatFusion, a novel architecture that enables this task by conditioning a diffusion model on both a 2D albedo texture and granular, PBR-style parametric controls, including roughness, metalness, transmission, and a key thickness parameter. Experiments and user studies show CoatFusion produces realistic, controllable coatings and significantly outperforms existing material editing and transfer methods on this new task.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Schr\"odinger's Navigator: Imagining an Ensemble of Futures for Zero-Shot Object Navigation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Zero-shot object navigation (ZSON) requires robots to find target objects in unseen environments without task-specific fine-tuning or pre-built maps, a key capability for general-purpose service robots. Yet methods that perform well in simulation often degrade in cluttered real-world scenes with severe occlusion and latent hazards, where large unseen regions make single-scene inference brittle and unsafe. We propose Schr\"odinger's Navigator, a belief-aware framework that reasons at inference time over multiple trajectory-conditioned imagined 3D futures. Given candidate paths, a trajectory-conditioned 3D world model predicts hypothetical observations and maintains a superposition of plausible scene realizations rather than committing to one map. An adaptive occluder-aware sampler directs imagination to uncertainty-critical regions, while a Future-Aware Value Map (FAVM) aggregates imagined futures for robust, proactive action selection. Experiments in simulation and on a physical Go2 quadruped show that Schr\"odinger's Navigator outperforms strong ZSON baselines, improving hidden-target discovery and risk-aware waypoint selection in occlusion-heavy navigation scenarios. These results highlight imagined 3D futures as a scalable and generalizable strategy for zero-shot navigation in uncertain real-world environments.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Happy Young Women, Grumpy Old Men? Emotion-Driven Demographic Biases in Synthetic Face Generation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Synthetic faces from text-to-image (T2I) models pervade digital media, yet their demographic biases under emotionally conditioned prompts remain poorly understood. We aim to systematically audit how emotionally conditioned prompts affect demographic and perceived-attractiveness biases in synthetic faces generated by T2I models, with particular attention to intersectional patterns and cross-ecosystem differences across model families. We audited eight (4 Western and 4 Chinese) T2I models and generated 56,000 faces under seven prompt conditions: a neutral baseline and six emotion conditions. We quantified biases in gender, race, age, and perceived attractiveness using information-theoretic divergence metrics. We further conducted intersectional analyses across combined demographic attributes and compared patterns between the Western and Chinese model groups to assess cross-ecosystem consistency and divergence in bias behavior. All models show strong overrepresentation of young faces, and most also overrepresent White-coded individuals. Intersectional analysis reveals compound underrepresentation or near-erasure of specific demographic combinations, such as young x female x Black faces, which are largely absent across models and are not captured by single-attribute audits. Emotion prompts act as additional demographic selectors: negatively valenced emotions (including sadness and fear) consistently shift outputs toward White, middle-aged, male-coded faces. This produces a valence-driven mapping that is also associated with lower perceived attractiveness in generated faces. These findings indicate that demographic bias in T2I face generation is both pervasive and shaped by emotional conditioning. They underscore the need for intersectional, emotion-conditioned, and multilingual demographic audits as part of standard pre-deployment evaluation practices.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: OMEGA-Avatar: One-shot Modeling of 360{\deg} Gaussian Avatars
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Creating high-fidelity, animatable 3D avatars from a single image remains a formidable challenge. We identified three desirable attributes of avatar generation: 1) the method should be feed-forward, 2) model a 360{\deg} full-head, and 3) should be animation-ready. However, current work addresses only two of the three points simultaneously. To address these limitations, we propose OMEGA-Avatar, the first feed-forward framework that simultaneously generates a generalizable, 360{\deg}-complete, and animatable 3D Gaussian head from a single image. Starting from a feed-forward and animatable framework, we address the 360{\deg} full-head avatar generation problem with two novel components. First, to overcome poor hair modeling in full-head avatar generation, we introduce a semantic-aware mesh deformation module that integrates multi-view normals to optimize a FLAME head with hair while preserving its topology structure. Second, to enable effective feed-forward decoding of full-head features, we propose a multi-view feature splatting module that constructs a shared canonical UV representation from features across multiple views through differentiable bilinear splatting, hierarchical UV mapping, and visibility-aware fusion. This approach preserves both global structural coherence and local high-frequency details across all viewpoints, ensuring 360{\deg} consistency without per-instance optimization. Extensive experiments demonstrate that OMEGA-Avatar achieves state-of-the-art performance, significantly outperforming existing baselines in 360{\deg} full-head completeness while robustly preserving identity across different viewpoints.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Differentiable design of the PIAA-ZWFS: a flexible wavefront sensor that approaches the fundamental limit
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Extreme adaptive optics (AO) is necessary for high contrast astronomy at scales of the habitable zone of nearby systems. We seek to evaluate wavefront sensors that approach fundamental limits of wavefront sensing, enabling adaptive optics systems to run faster or on fainter targets. We present the phase-induced amplitude apodisation Zernike wavefront sensor (PIAA-ZWFS): an adaptation of the conventional Zernike wavefront sensor (ZWFS) that leverages lossless apodisation of the pupil to concentrate the starlight in the focal plane. We optimise and evaluate the sensor with a differentiable modelling framework, drawing on concepts from Bayesian experimental design to minimise the variance of a maximum likelihood estimator that uses the system in the high Strehl regime. Our architecture shows state-of-the-art performance in simulation for different apertures, bandwidths, photon fluxes and source sizes, closing the gap to the fundamental limit by a factor 10 (2.5) compared to the conventional ZWFS (optimised ZWFS) in a typical photon-limited case. For extended sources, we show that even an ideal point source sensor rapidly becomes sub-optimal, and our system outperforms it for stellar diameters larger than 0.8{\lambda}/D. We verify that these gains do not come at the cost of dynamic range with either linear or non-linear reconstructors. Finally, we present a proof that there must be a trade-off between the information gained about amplitude and phase errors for any wavefront sensor. The PIAA-ZWFS is a viable wavefront sensor operating near the fundamental sensitivity limits.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Rescene: stable century-long climate emulation from a frozen weather model
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Machine-learning weather models now match or exceed operational numerical prediction in the medium range, but when they are run freely for years they drift, blow up or lose their variability, and dedicated climate emulators are expensive to train. Here we present Rescene, a 0.4 M-parameter wrapper that turns a frozen 1.5$^\circ$, 6-hourly, 69-variable weather model into a stochastic climate emulator. A deterministic slow clock anchors the frozen model to a calendar climatology, and a band-limited AR(1) perturbation, whose spectral envelope is fixed to the observed anomaly spectrum, restores the weather that anchoring removes. A 100-year, 8-member Rescene run shows no detectable drift ($-0.004 \pm 0.014$ K per 100 years), and on the 2022 test year the 16-member ensemble is calibrated (spread/skill 0.89, 0.97 and 0.93 for Z500, T2m and MSLP) with an extratropical synoptic amplitude of 97% of ERA5 on the tuning year. The free run reproduces the geography of day-to-day variability (pattern correlation 0.83 for Z500) and 71% of the observed blocking frequency, where the deterministic wrapper alone has none. Interventions on the frozen operator show a scale-local, approximately linear response in which Z500 perturbations grow upscale 6--14 times more than downscale per 6 h. All constants are fitted on a training year against a rule declared beforehand, and we show that common evaluation shortcuts would have overstated variability and skill. Rescene makes an existing weather model usable for century-long ensembles at negligible training cost.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: MeshSuite: A Unified Benchmark for Triangle- and Mesh-Based Neural Rendering
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering seeks to bridge neural representations and graphics engines through triangle primitives compatible with standard rasterization. Yet existing methods were developed and evaluated under inconsistent settings, with few direct comparisons and little evaluation in graphics engines. We introduce MeshSuite, the first benchmark for systematic evaluation of engine deployment and Non-Engine Render in triangle- and mesh-based neural rendering. MeshSuite evaluates two deployment settings: Standard Deployment, using an opaque mesh pipeline with vertex colors and hardware Z-buffering; and Dedicated Deployment, using method-specific engine implementations to preserve appearance and compositing features. For mesh splatting, we also audit exported surfaces for topological and geometric integrity as downstream graphics assets. Our results show that engine deployment reduces image quality in both settings; among evaluated methods, MeshSplatting degrades least under Standard Deployment. Dedicated Deployment preserves most fidelity at roughly 5-33x the runtime of Standard Deployment across two deployment datasets. For mesh splatting, explicit connectivity and shared indexing remain limited: shared vertex indexing alone guarantees neither manifoldness nor global connectivity. These findings show that rasterizability is only part of graphics readiness and underscore the need to assess engine deployment. Project page: https://surrey-up-lab.github.io/MeshSuite.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: TV-AudioRemover: Joint Text-Visual Guided Sound Removal with Multi-Task Hard-Mixture Curriculum
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Visual object removal can eliminate a target from video frames, yet its acoustic trace persists in the soundtrack, causing obvious audio-visual inconsistency. Existing video inpainting models operate solely on pixels, while audio editing models, especially for the sound removal task, are typically driven by text and therefore rely on limited single-modal control, which is less effective than multimodal guidance that provides stronger semantic grounding and temporal synchronization cues. In this paper, we present Text-Visual Guided Sound Removal (TV-AudioRemover), a target sound removal framework that leverages the visually edited video together with a natural-language instruction to suppress the sound associated with the removed visual object from the original audio mixture. To acquire high-quality training data, we devise a pipeline to construct a million-scale dataset of single-object audio-visual aligned samples, from which we synthesize mixture-target pairs customized for model training. To effectively leverage visual context and follow instruction intent, we augment the model architecture with task tokens, generalizable instruction modeling, and modality-specific global guidance. We further adopt multi-task training to strengthen task-role comprehension, and employ a hard-mixture curriculum that leverages semantically similar acoustic mixtures during fine-tuning to enhance fine-grained source discrimination. To support evaluation, we present AV-Remove-Bench, a comprehensive audio-visual object removal benchmark, along with dedicated objective metrics and an MLLM-based evaluation protocol. Experiments demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on both subjective and objective metrics. Project page: https://yjx-research.github.io/TV-AudioRemover/.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Learnable Spectral Activations
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Implicit neural representations (INRs) are shaped by the spectral structure induced by their input encodings and activation functions. Existing methods improve fitting primarily by modifying which frequencies are available to the network, through coordinate encodings or periodic nonlinearities. However, frequency access is not the only bottleneck: signals with localized or spatially varying structure require the network to efficiently compose frequencies into multi-harmonic internal responses. We introduce learnable spectral activations (LSA), which replace fixed neuron-level nonlinearities with a residual truncated Fourier series whose harmonic amplitudes are learned during training. LSA does not expand the asymptotic function class. Instead, it changes the factorization of the representation: linear weights select features while activation coefficients control spectral shaping, and the two are updated by separate gradients. Because the activation output is affine in the coefficients given fixed pre-activations, spectral tuning becomes a more direct subproblem compared to architectures where it is entangled with feature selection. Empirically, this factorization concentrates more target-signal energy in the leading eigenmodes of the neural tangent kernel, consistent with improved optimization behavior. Across audio, image, neural radiance field, and neural acoustic field tasks, LSA also improves reconstruction quality.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Bernoulli Flow Models: Self-Consistent Generative Modeling for Binary Data
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Binary diffusion models typically require many function evaluations (NFEs) to generate high-quality samples, making inference costly. Reducing NFEs without sacrificing sample quality or relying on distillation or additional training remains challenging. Existing binary diffusion models define discrete one-step forward paths and derive reverse posteriors accordingly. In low-NFE cross-step sampling, they incorrectly approximate a true multi-step likelihood using a single-step transition, causing severe quality degradation. We propose Bernoulli Flow Models (BFM) to decouple generative dynamics from fixed discrete time steps. Instead of sequential one-step Markov diffusion chains, BFM defines a unified continuous global Bernoulli probability flow path between data and pure noise and derives analytical closed-form posterior transitions over arbitrary time intervals. Reducing the inference NFE therefore only requires re-evaluating this posterior on the new intervals rather than approximating skipped steps. This removes the structural training-inference mismatch of discrete chains and enables strictly self-consistent low-NFE sampling. Experiments show strong robustness under aggressive NFE reduction: on LSUN Churches 256x256, a 256-step-trained BFM achieves an FID of 9.22 with only 16 sampling steps, while the state-of-the-art discrete baseline degrades to 204.10. BFM also remains competitive with continuous and discrete generative baselines under standard full-step inference. These results establish BFM as a theoretically rigorous, self-consistent, and practical framework for fast binary data generation. Code is available at https://github.com/minimo6666/BFM_NeurIPS2026.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: MultiWorldBench: Do Independently Controlled Views Describe One Shared World?
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Multiplayer world models must ensure that independently controlled views remain consistent with a single shared and persistent world. We introduce MultiWorldBench, a diagnostic Minecraft benchmark comprising 495 case configurations across seven task suites and ten capabilities, including independent control, cross-view motion, shared-state synchronization, persistence, structural reasoning, concurrent interaction, and delayed revisit. Using Engine GT as a reference, we evaluate two multiplayer world models, Solaris (MP) and Gamma-World, together with a single-player generation variant, Solaris (SP). Among the generated systems, Gamma-World achieves the highest ten-capability average at 21.39, followed by Solaris (MP) at 20.88 and Solaris (SP) at 10.06, while Engine GT reaches 91.69. Gamma-World performs better on several control, shared-state, and revisit capabilities, whereas Solaris (MP) leads in cross-view motion and race-condition consistency. Nevertheless, all generated systems score at most 8.00 on state persistence and 1.33 on structural consistency, and none succeeds in spatial reasoning or building-identity preservation. Human pairwise evaluation yields the same overall system ranking and shows strong alignment with the automatic evaluation, with a mean dimension-level Spearman correlation of 0.95. These results show that current multiplayer world models still exhibit a substantial gap relative to Engine GT in maintaining a coherent shared world.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Hybrid Cinematography: Previsualizing and Managing Hallucination Risk in Generative Video Reshooting
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: On a film set, the camera move is committed during a take. Generative video reshooting lets filmmakers change it afterward, but may require hallucinating unrecorded content, a gap sometimes discovered only after leaving the set. We present Hybrid Cinematography, a workflow that bridges physical capture and generative reshooting to manage hallucination risk while filmmakers can still act on it. Using an editable 3D shot plan and a proxy of the take, our previsualization evaluates hallucination risk in real time. Seeing where the take lacks support, filmmakers can iteratively adjust the plan, explore moves that balance capture and generation, shoot guided pickups, or knowingly accept hallucination. We demonstrate the workflow through a mobile augmented reality application for on-set planning, capture, and review, and an offline pipeline for existing video. A study with experienced filmmakers reveals how previsualizing risk informs camera decisions and exposes tensions between creative intent and generative hallucination.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: WorldOracle: Benchmarking Action-Conditioned World Models against Real-World Executions
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: We introduce WorldOracle, a benchmark specifically designed to evaluate action-conditioned world models (ACWMs) against paired real-world executions. Given the same initial observation and low-level action sequence, WorldOracle asks whether a predicted rollout reproduces what happens in the real world, including physical consequences and task-state transitions. We evaluate models along four complementary dimensions: physical state correctness, interaction spatial alignment, key interaction area fidelity, and multi-view action coherence. To support this evaluation, we curate real-world training and evaluation suites that cover different interaction dynamics and embodiments. The evaluation suite contains long, multi-segment episodes with both successful and failed executions, enabling evaluation across varied action outcomes and behavior distributions. Experiments on seven representative ACWMs reveal distinct model strengths and failure modes. WorldOracle provides a systematic foundation for measuring and advancing action-conditioned world modeling for manipulation. We release the datasets, evaluation code, and leaderboard: https://worldoracle-benchmark.github.io/.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Riding the Fixed-Point Curve: Image Classification in the Continuous Thought Machine
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: The Continuous Thought Machine (CTM) is a recurrent network that attends to inputs and makes predictions based on the synchronization between its neurons. On tasks spanning many domains, it displays emergent thought processes that have not been explained. We report a number of findings about how the CTM classifies images, focusing on ImageNet. Thinking steps are attracting but strongly non-normal maps exhibiting balanced amplification (Murphy and Miller, 2009); while attraction is already present at CTM initialization, training highly promotes non-normality. By Banach's theorem, the neural state thus has a locally unique attracting fixed point, which moves at every step, and the thought trajectory is the curve these fixed points trace, followed one tick behind. Most of that curve's motion is shared across images, and visible as a previously reported traveling wave of activity across neurons. The attention schedule along the thought is largely generic: shuffling queries across images at every tick costs only 7 percent of classification accuracy, while image-independent increments predict the next query with R^2 = 0.98 (held out). Our results suggest that the CTM has found a single strategy to process all ImageNet images.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: ActiveEvidence: Decision-Focused Evidence Graphs with Verifiable Acquisition Gaps
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: A multimodal agent must decide whether visual evidence is worth acquiring, which candidate or resolution to query, and when further interaction can no longer change its decision. We study this problem under a strict free-metadata/paid-observation boundary, stochastic vector costs, and a frozen execution trace, and treat it as decision-certifiable active evidence acquisition. A Counterfactual Evidence Interaction Graph (CEIG) represents unary evidence value, signed second-order interaction, and directed conditional harm while maintaining explicit score enclosures for unresolved interactions; a decision-weighted enclosure objective tightens the bounds that can change action identity. Gap-directed refinement evaluates only interactions that can displace the incumbent acquisition and stops once an $\epsilon$-decision certificate shows that unresolved terms cannot change the selected action beyond a declared tolerance. The certificate is model-relative: it verifies policy-consistent optimality under the pinned learned score, and semantic quality is measured separately through post-freeze labels. Paired continuation rollouts learn the downstream value of paid previews, an online operational cost filter is separated from independent finite-policy-family trajectory certification, and an acquisition monitor with an independently implemented verifier binds every certificate to the frozen trace. On 640 cases split into 384/128/128 training, validation, and test cases, the controller reaches task score 0.842, grounding F1 0.816, evidence recall 0.873, 1.74 accepted calls, 286.5K visual tokens, and 742ms p95 latency. Dense replay of issued certificates shows 0.992 action agreement and a 0.988 certificate rate while evaluating 19.6 instead of 191.4 expensive interaction terms per decision.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Learnable Hodge-Laplacian Driven Mixture of Experts for Steady-PDE Surrogates on Coarse Unstructured Meshes
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Current approaches for steady partial differential equations surrogate models on unstructured meshes apply a single mixing mechanism to the whole solution. This paper proposes an architecture that partitions the solution among vanilla transformer experts, each focused on a different spectral scale. The partition is built from a discrete Hodge Laplacian $L_0=\star_0^{-1} d_0^{\top}\star_1 d_0$, that serves as a fitting layer measuring high-frequency content. A gating mechanism takes the mesh as input and produces the per-vertex weights that recombine the expert outputs. AirFRANS is a steady Reynolds-averaged Navier--Stokes (RANS) airfoil benchmark. We evaluate our approach in a reduced remeshed version of the benchmark with each unstructured mesh counting 9.6K faces and 4.9K vertices. We compare our approach with the Transolver on the same dataset and dataset slit. Our approach reduces relative $L_2$ error by 31% and interior mean squared error by 47%.

Robotics.title: DUET: Decoupled Upper- and Lower-Body Execution for Task-Agnostic Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
Robotics.summary: Changing a humanoid robot's manipulation policy should not require retraining the controller that maintains the robot's balance. This study introduces DUET, a decoupled execution framework that enables locomotion and manipulation controllers to operate simultaneously by combining their commands only at the robot interface. A reinforcement-learning locomotion policy controls the 12 leg joints and a waist yaw joint, tracking planar velocity, turning rate, and pelvis height from deep crouching to upright standing on a 23-degree-of-freedom Unitree G1. The 10 arm joints are excluded from the action space, while their positions and velocities are included only as observations, so that any compatible manipulation policy that generates arm-joint targets can control the upper body, and the locomotion policy keeps the lower body stable without requiring shared training or direct coordination. This study demonstrates the modular approach on hardware by pairing the same locomotion checkpoint with two different vision-language-action models, GR00T N1.7 and pi0.5. In simulation evaluation, the locomotion controller kept the robot's lower body stable with no falls while tracking the commanded planar velocity, yaw rate, and pelvis height with errors of 0.186 m/s, 0.142 rad/s, and 0.016 m, respectively. Ablation studies identify the upper-body pose curriculum as the dominant component, and removing this training step reduces episode survival from 20.0 to 7.4 seconds and increases the fall rate to 6.06 per environment minute. Robustness tests show no falls under pushes of up to 1.0 m/s within the trained payload range, and no falls at twice the payload limit for pushes below 0.7 m/s. These results show that a manipulation policy can be exchanged without retraining, restarting, or otherwise touching the layer that keeps the robot upright.

Robotics.title: Context-Aware RGB-Thermal-Radar Obstacle Perception for Resource-Constrained ASVs
Robotics.summary: Reliable obstacle perception is challenging for small autonomous surface vessels (ASVs): reflections and glare confound visible-light cameras, vessel motion shifts the apparent waterline, and darkness removes the dominant sensing modality altogether. Rather than treating multimodal fusion as a static accuracy gain, we propose a context-aware architecture that combines RGB and long-wave infrared (LWIR) imagery, frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW) mmWave radar, and inertial context. A bearing-sector interface provides the navigation controller with calibrated obstacle probabilities, radar ranges, and sensor status. It also distinguishes sensor dropout from a valid observation with no detected obstacle. Using new multimodal lake recordings, we deployed the pipeline in a 24-leg closed-loop pilot under uncontrolled lake conditions (16 day, 4 dusk, and 4 night; 351 m), including night legs in which RGB was unusable and the vessel drove on LWIR and radar evidence alone. On eight held-out low-light recordings, the calibrated fusion model achieved average precision (AP) 0.869 and expected calibration error 0.108, compared with AP 0.673 for rule-based fusion, 0.620 for gated fusion, and 0.903 for RGB alone. Our results expose a central tradeoff: RGB ranks best when usable, whereas fusion preserves a navigation input when RGB fails. This work is a step toward perception that remains usable and degrades predictably across multi-day ASV missions.

Robotics.title: Adaptive Question Generation for Ambiguous Robot Instructions Based on Information Gain and Human Cognitive Characteristics
Robotics.summary: In this study, we propose an adaptive question generation mechanism that addresses uncertainty arising from ambiguous instructions. Natural-language instructions for service robots often contain ambiguities. In scenes with multiple similar objects, the robot must identify the target object by asking questions. However, existing question generation methods focus on probabilistic discrimination efficiency and do not sufficiently account for user ease of response. Asking questions without considering the user's ease of response may cause incorrect or uncertain answers. Such incorrect or uncertain answers lead to additional clarification turns and degraded dialogue efficiency. The proposed mechanism integrates probabilistic discrimination efficiency and human cognitive characteristics to generate questions that users can intuitively and easily answer. First, the proposed mechanism extracts visual attributes of candidate objects using a vision-language model (VLM). Next, the proposed mechanism computes the information gain (IG) of each attribute and selects the visual attribute (e.g., color, shape) that most reduces uncertainty in the candidate set. When multiple attributes have the same IG, the proposed mechanism applies a visual attribute filter based on cognitive characteristics to select the visual attribute that users can most intuitively perceive. The proposed mechanism then prompts the VLM with the selected attribute and the corresponding attribute values of each candidate object to generate a concise natural-language question. This process is repeated until the target object is uniquely identified. The proposed mechanism achieved a target identification success rate of 88.5% in the evaluation using a dataset of 120 scenes. Furthermore, the proposed mechanism received high ratings in subjective evaluations of response ease.

Robotics.title: Stress-Query and Temporal Reliability of Vision-Language Models as copilots in Autonomous UAV Navigation
Robotics.summary: Integrating Vision-Language Models (VLMs) into autonomous UAV navigation enables high-level semantic reasoning but introduces critical temporal bottlenecks that can destabilize flight control. This paper presents a systematic benchmark that evaluates the operational trade-offs among model scale, hardware constraints, and flight reliability. By subjecting the system to extensive stress tests on both a high-performance workstation and a constrained integrated-graphics laptop, we isolate the kinetic impact of inference latency against reasoning accuracy. Our findings reveal a performance dichotomy: lightweight models struggle with structural hallucinations that break deterministic state machines, while heavyweight models induce trajectory overcorrections due to inference lag. We demonstrate that a mid-weight architecture strikes the optimal balance, successfully rehabilitating navigation in degraded environments without compromising real-time stability across different hardware profiles.

Robotics.title: A Heterogeneous UAV UGV Methodology for Aerial Tracking of Mini Autonomous Cars
Robotics.summary: Aerial tracking of autonomous ground vehicles can provide useful situational awareness in environments where fixed external perception infrastructure is unavailable. However, visual-only tracking from an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) is limited by camera field of view, viewpoint changes, occlusions, and temporary loss of target visibility. This paper presents a heterogeneous UAV--UGV methodology for aerial tracking of small-scale autonomous ground vehicles in simulation. The system is implemented in ROS~2 and Gazebo Sim using a Tello-like UAV equipped with a front-facing RGB camera and multiple LIMO-like unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs). Three approaches are evaluated: a training-free color-marker baseline, a YOLO-based visual baseline, and a proposed UAV--UGV fusion method. The proposed method uses the same visual detector as the YOLO baseline, but combines visual detections with UGV state information to maintain the target estimate during visual gaps. The methods are evaluated across four scenarios: single-car tracking, crossing trajectories, occlusion, and UAV-assisted awareness. Results over 600 simulation runs show that the proposed fusion method achieves nearly continuous track coverage across all scenarios while reducing localization error relative to the YOLO baseline. Compared with the visual-only YOLO approach, the fusion method reduces RMSE by 37.3\%, 64.2\%, 62.6\%, and 61.8\% in the four evaluated scenarios, respectively. The method also enables conflict-awareness lead times of 10.20~s in the crossing scenario and 9.07~s in the UAV-assisted awareness scenario. These results indicate that heterogeneous UAV--UGV fusion can improve aerial tracking continuity and robustness when visual observations are intermittent.

Robotics.title: Adaptive Rejection of Unknown Hybrid Sinusoidal Disturbances with Application to Humanoid Walking under Unknown Ground Motion
Robotics.summary: Legged robot control is not yet practical in non-inertial environments, where the ground and surroundings accelerate in the inertial Earth frame, mainly because of the unknown, time-varying, persistent perturbations caused by environmental motion, compounded by the associated hybrid robotic dynamics. We formulate the problem of robot walking control as unknown-disturbance rejection for hybrid linear systems subject to hybrid sinusoidal disturbances (i.e., a linear combination of sinusoidal components with instantaneous phase jumps at discrete events). First, necessary and sufficient conditions for solvability of the disturbance rejection problem are derived and used to characterize the control input that rejects the disturbances. Second, with the Youla-Kucera parametrization, an output feedback controller capable of rejecting the disturbance is introduced. Third, an adaptive law is proposed to estimate the controller parameters that reject the disturbance in the practical case where the disturbance and its parameters are unknown. Experiments on bipedal walking during ground motion demonstrate substantially improved body-position tracking accuracy, with an average improvement of over 60% in simulations and up to 47% in real-world experiments.

Robotics.title: AutoPruner: Agentic Depth Pruning for Vision-Language-Action Models
Robotics.summary: Layer pruning reduces the size and inference cost of vision-language-action (VLA) models, but selecting a deployable configuration requires deciding both which layers to remove and how to recover task performance. These decisions depend on the model and task, and a failed trial can reflect either the deletion set or insufficient recovery. We present AutoPruner, an agent-driven framework that jointly searches pruning structures and recovery recipes through closed-loop experimentation. Offline layer interventions measure changes in action output to provide functional evidence. An LLM agent combines this evidence with evaluation history and retained diagnoses to propose deletion sets and recovery recipes within a search budget. Each proposal is executed and evaluated on the target tasks, and the resulting feedback guides the next experiment. Across OpenVLA-OFT, StarVLA, and FastWAM on four LIBERO suites, AutoPruner removes 16.7--87.5% of backbone layers while maintaining task success above 90%, with measured inference speedups of up to 2.50$\times$. Further analysis shows that functional probes identify action-sensitive layers despite high representation similarity, and that recovery can make previously failing structures viable.

Robotics.title: Learning Whole-Body Kinetic Coordination for Wheeled-Quadruped Long-Range Throwing
Robotics.summary: Long-range throwing on unstructured terrain is a key capability for mobile robots in delivery and retrieval tasks, but it requires high release velocity, coordinated whole-body motion, and robustness to terrain-induced disturbances. We present a whole-body kinetic-coordination framework for a wheeled-quadruped manipulator that combines kinetic-chain arm modeling with SQP-based trajectory optimization and a reference-guided reinforcement learning policy for coordinated base motion. The manipulator is first reduced to a kinetic-chain model and optimized under kinematic and dynamic constraints to produce a high-speed throwing reference. On a stationary base, the optimized arm trajectory reaches a release speed of 12.75 m/s and a throwing distance of 16.68 m. When whole-body coordination is enabled, the system further increases the release speed to 16.64 m/s and the throwing distance to 28.25 m. We then integrate the mobility of the wheeled-quadruped platform and validate the complete policy through hardware experiments on flat ground, grass, slopes, and rough roads. The results show that kinetic-chain optimization and whole-body coordination together enable robust long-range throwing across diverse unstructured terrains.

Robotics.title: PrismPlan: A Shared GPU Substrate for Motion Planning Across Paradigms
Robotics.summary: GPU acceleration has made motion planning one to two orders of magnitude faster, but it has not made the three paradigms---sampling, search, and optimization---comparable to one another: every GPU-accelerated planner is built around a single paradigm, so comparing across libraries also compares their collision checkers. All three, however, bottleneck on the same GPU primitive: batched collision detection and the batched forward kinematics beneath it. PrismPlan builds that primitive once, as a shared substrate of per-sphere collision--kinematics device code that every planner consumes. Because they all execute the same device code, the backend is held fixed by construction and the paradigms can be compared head-to-head. We run six planners over 1800 MotionBenchMaker problems on three robots (7--14 DoF, one a dual-arm whole-body composite) at an equal 2s budget. On the 7-DoF Panda, sampling (pRRTC) is the most reliable paradigm at 98%, while parallel search (wPA*SE) follows within four points at a 3-4 times$ lower median latency, and the local optimizers trail well behind when made to solve from scratch. On the 14-DoF dual-arm composite, sampling still solves about 90% of feasible problems, while no search or optimization planner clears a third of them. Our open-source code is available at https://github.com/XiaoyubotMotionTeam/PrismPlan.

Robotics.title: From Likelihood to Utility: Quality-Axis Diffusion for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
Robotics.summary: Diffusion models have become a dominant paradigm for end-to-end autonomous driving, yet existing planners organize trajectory generation along the Gaussian-noise axis, treating driving utility only as an auxiliary guidance or selection signal. We instead formulate diffusion along a driving-quality axis. We propose QualiDrive, which constructs scene-specific quality ladders by ranking observed trajectories according to measured driving utility and learns to reverse this ordered degradation through ordered low-to-high-quality refinement. Each reverse step is conditioned on the scene, ego state, current trajectory, and target quality level, progressively refining trajectories toward higher driving quality. On NAVSIM, QualiDrive achieves 94.5 PDMS on v1 and a state-of-the-art 92.74 EPDMS on v2. QualiDrive improves Oracle EPDMS only modestly over endpoint-only quality supervision (98.52 to 98.57), but substantially increases the fractions of candidates above 0.95 and 0.98 EPDMS from 12.94%/9.71% to 21.53%/15.93%, raising selected EPDMS from 92.63 to 92.74. These results suggest that diffusion is not merely a process of denoising, but one of progressive quality-ordered refinement.

Robotics.title: EvoAD: Self-Evolving Autonomous Driving via Latent World-Model Guided Post-hoc Reflection
Robotics.summary: End-to-end autonomous driving systems have achieved rapid progress by learning unified policies that map sensor observations directly to driving trajectories. However, once deployed, these systems typically remain frozen: they may repeat similar decisions in similar scenes, and failures can only be addressed through costly data collection and retraining. This sharply contrasts with human drivers, who improve lifelong through experience, memory, and reflection. In this work, we ask whether autonomous driving systems can achieve similar post-deployment self-evolution to human drivers. We propose EvoAD, a self-evolving autonomous driving framework via latent world-model guided post-hoc reflection. EvoAD stores driving experiences in a bird's-eye-view feature memory pool, retrieves scene-relevant precedents according to geometric and semantic similarity, and uses a latent world model to evaluate the future consequences of candidate trajectories in a compact planning-oriented space. Instead of treating memory as external textual contexts or using world models only for pre-action simulation, EvoAD transforms executed driving outcomes into reusable improvement signals for future decisions. This enables the system to diagnose how prior trajectories could have been improved and to refine behavior in similar future scenarios without retraining the base driving policy. Experiments on NAVSIM v1 and v2 show consistent improvements across reflection rounds and state-of-the-art performance, demonstrating the potential of world models as reflective mechanisms for post-deployment self-evolution in autonomous driving.

Robotics.title: ContactKernels: Adaptive Proposals using Geometry-COnditioned Wrenches for Contact-Rich Manipulation
Robotics.summary: Contact-rich insertion requires precise geometric alignment despite uncertainty in perception, geometry, and con- trol. When this uncertainty causes unintended contact, the re- sulting contact provides local information that can guide correc- tive motion. Sampling-based Model Predictive Control (SMPC) is well suited to this setting because it optimizes through forward simulation without requiring gradients through contact dynamics. However, standard SMPC methods typically use generic proposal distributions that do not exploit observed contact to determine where to search next. We introduce ContactKernels, a contact-adaptive proposal kernel that uses geometry-conditioned wrench measurements to estimate contact location and local contact geometry. The estimated contact state directly adapts the proposal distribution: contact location biases the search toward corrective motions, while the contact normal shapes the sampling covariance. We evaluate ContactKernels with Predictive Sampling (PS) and Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI) control across multiple insertion geometries in simulation and on a real robot. In simulation, ContactKernels improves mean insertion success by over 50 % points across both controllers. On the real robot, it increases insertion success from 53.3 % to 90.0 % and reduces mean time to insertion by 33 %. These results show that contact information can improve sampling-based control not only as feedback, but also by directly determining where the controller searches

Robotics.title: MoDex: Towards Universal Multi-Object Dexterous Grasping
Robotics.summary: Multi-object grasping is a fundamental yet challenging problem, constrained by data collection costs, varying spatial layouts, and the need for broad generalization. To address these challenges, we propose MoDex, a data-efficient framework that provides the first unified solution for universal multi-object dexterous grasping across diverse spatial layouts. MoDex accomplishes this by formulating the task as a single-step decision problem of learning residual corrections to a reference trajectory, and introducing a spatially adaptive dual-strategy that performs single-shot grasping for proximal objects and sequential interaction for separated objects. Extensive evaluations show that MoDex significantly outperforms baselines in proximal configurations, achieving 61.24% success on unseen objects, and achieves high success rates in separated layouts. Further experiments demonstrate its generalization across robot embodiments, scalability and zero-shot sim-to-real deployment through a vision-based policy trained solely on simulation data. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/Aurora-Xiong/MoDex.

Robotics.title: When to Make a Decision: Task-Sufficient Active Perception for Mobile Manipulator Robots
Robotics.summary: A robotic agent operating in an unknown environment must gather sufficient task-relevant information before acting. However, determining when the available information is sufficient remains a challenge. We propose a conceptual hybrid neuro-symbolic framework for task-sufficient active perception in unknown environments. After interpreting a requested task, the agent generates an initial plan and iteratively reevaluates it as new information becomes available. At each iteration, it can acquire a more informative viewpoint, inspect or manipulate candidate objects, ask the user for clarification, or perform the task. Neural perception modules update an object-centric belief state, while a symbolic decision layer determines whether the remaining uncertainty justifies further information gathering. The framework will be implemented on a mobile manipulator comprising a humanoid torso and a mobile base, with complementary evaluation in simulation. The proposed approach aims to enable robots to determine not only how to gather additional information, but also when further perception is no longer necessary.

Robotics.title: Language-Forcing: Advancing Humanoid Loco-Manipulation via Semantic Alignment of Whole-Body World Action Models
Robotics.summary: World Action Models (WAMs) jointly predict robot actions and future observations. However, their visual prediction objectives do not explicitly distinguish task-relevant transitions from incidental scene changes. For whole-body policies, this distinction matters because task progress depends on coordinated changes in body pose, contact, and object state. We introduce LANGUAGE-FORCING, a training strategy that uses language to emphasize task-relevant changes in the future visual representations of a whole-body WAM. Given paired current and ground- truth short-horizon future frames, a frozen vision-language model assesses task progress and predicts plausible subsequent state changes. We encode these descriptions with a frozen text encoder and align their embeddings with intermediate, action-conditioned future-visual features, complementing the original visual and action prediction objectives. All auxiliary components are used only during training, introducing no additional inference overhead. On HumanoidArena, LANGUAGE-FORCING achieves an average success rate of 79.17%, exceeding the strongest competing policy by 9.46 percentage points and the same WAM without language alignment by 10.77 percentage points. Across five real-world tasks, language alignment raises average success from 53.33% to 71.33% over the same WAM baseline.

Robotics.title: InJePA: Intention-First Latent Planning with Coupled JEPA World Models for Visual Navigation
Robotics.summary: Visual navigation requires goal directed planning informed by predictions of environment dynamics. Representative navigation world model methods propose complete action candidates before predicting consequences for selection or search updates. For each candidate, predictions primarily evaluate proposed actions rather than guide its stepwise construction. To this end, we propose InJepa, an intention first planning paradigm centered on latent states. A goal conditioned JEPA proposes latent intentions, and an action conditioned JEPA continually predicts future latent states. Both operate in a shared latent space to align their predictive representations. Within each candidate, predicted consequences feed into the next intention proposal and action inference, forming a closed loop of intention, action, and consequence. This extends the world model's role beyond evaluation to leading candidate construction through latent intentions. We evaluate InJepa through closed loop image goal navigation in Habitat MP3D. The results show effective multistep navigation through intention guided action generation and consequence feedback. Experiments across encoders further support applicability across visual representations. These findings support latent intentions as the central planning object and show that world models can directly guide plan construction through coordinated reasoning about intentions and consequences. Code is available at https://github.com/zhuxun132/InJepa.

Robotics.title: MicroSplat: Towards Automating 3D Small-Scale Reconstruction
Robotics.summary: Reconstructing sub-millimeter detail of small objects underpins tasks such as circuit-board defect detection, specimen digitization, and archiving. 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) makes photorealistic reconstruction possible from posed images alone, but macro optics violate two conditions it depends on. The field of view (FOV) and the depth of field (DoF) shrink to millimeters, so viewpoint error can take a sample out of frame, and only a thin focal plane is sharp in frame. Existing automated macro-capture rigs handle the shallow DoF with per-view focus stacking, but typically rely on classical photogrammetry and offline, human-in-the-loop processing. We present MicroSplat, which generates a 3DGS using a low-cost consumer microscope on a manipulator arm. After a single up-front object-localization step, the system runs unattended. It performs calibration, plans collision-free viewpoints, captures and fuses a focal stack at each viewpoint, segments the object across all views, and optimizes a 3DGS model warm-started with the arm's own poses. We further compare against blur-aware 3DGS methods, which infer sharp scenes from defocused images, and find that measuring sharpness with a controlled focal sweep outperforms inferring it. We provide real and synthetic datasets (including robot and camera parameters) and the fitted 3DGS reconstructions.

Robotics.title: UMI-WM: Interactive World Modeling for Bimanual Manipulation from Wrist Cameras
Robotics.summary: Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) pairs wrist-camera videos with camera trajectories and gripper openings, providing scalable, robot-free data for learning how bimanual actions change a shared scene. Existing interactive world models, however, typically rely on text or single-camera control and struggle to follow each arm's actions while maintaining consistency between the two wrist views. We introduce UMI-WM, an action-conditioned bimanual world model that jointly generates both wrist views from observation history, per-arm relative camera poses, and gripper widths, with cross-view consistency, action following, and visual fidelity. UMI-WM injects each arm's actions into its own wrist stream, while sparse hub tokens exchange scene information between the two streams. Camera-aware geometry conditioning and camera-guided noise further support per-view motion control and cross-view geometric exchange. We adapt the model for block-causal generation and distill the 30-step Teacher into a Student with four denoising steps. We train UMI-WM on self-collected open-world and in-studio UMI recordings combined with public manipulation data. To evaluate action following, we use an inverse dynamics model (IDM) to recover relative camera poses and gripper widths from generated videos, and introduce Bimanual Action Fidelity (BAF) to measure how closely these recovered actions match the conditioning actions. UMI-WM achieves the best results on all five reference-video fidelity metrics and the best or competitive performance on VBench and WorldArena. The Teacher and Student outperform all compared baselines in action following, while the four-step Student generates paired wrist videos 6.9 times faster than the Teacher.

Robotics.title: ESCAPE: Egocentric Sensing for Collision Avoidance and Policy Execution
Robotics.summary: Motion planning in unstructured environments is a bottleneck for robot deployment. Current visuomotor policies predominantly rely on external cameras, introducing perceptual blind spots and fragility due to occlusions, clutter, and calibration constraints. To overcome these limitations, we propose ESCAPE, an online egocentric sensing framework for collision-free trajectory generation. ESCAPE aggregates sparse measurements from distributed depth sensors, converting them into a structured, obstacle-aware point cloud representation. Our policy leverages a flow matching-based generative framework, and trains on a high-quality dataset comprising over 100K safety-critical trajectories. With joint optimization of goal-reaching and collision objectives, it produces safe trajectories directly from these egocentric inputs. Crucially, ESCAPE is trained entirely in simulation and transfers zero-shot to physical hardware without any real-world fine-tuning. Extensive simulation and real-world evaluations demonstrate that ESCAPE achieves stable motion planning using only egocentric perception, outperforming external-view and voxelized-planning baselines across both simulation and real-world evaluations.

Robotics.title: REAP: Learning General Rearrangement Heuristics from Motion-Planner Feedback
Robotics.summary: Robotic rearrangement tasks require planning sequences of actions that fulfill high-level specifications while also being geometrically feasible. Symbolic abstractions make the combinatorial structure of rearrangement tasks tractable, but they usually do not fully capture the geometric constraints that determine which actions a robot can actually realize. These constraints are hard to express in the symbolic model. We propose REAP (Rearrangement with Elicited Action Preconditions), a framework in which a relational graph neural network heuristic is learned over a simple symbolic abstraction. A motion planner serves as a supervisor that elicits the hidden geometric preconditions of the problem during training. Deployed with greedy best-first search, the learned heuristic generalizes out-of-distribution along object count, plan length, and object arrangement, and can be trained jointly on several domains. Compared to classical heuristic search and learning-based baselines, REAP solves more problems, requires roughly an order of magnitude fewer motion-planner queries than comparable methods, and the action it ranks first is geometrically feasible in 94% of sampled states, against 22% for a random choice.

Robotics.title: Weakly Supervised Discovery of Motion Styles for Compositional Robot Control
Robotics.summary:
When a robot possesses more degrees of freedom than a task requires, multiple trajectories can achieve the same objective using distinct motion styles. Compositional robot control aims to preserve a selected style while simultaneously executing an independent task command, effectively balancing these potentially competing objectives. In this paper, we present CODES, a framework for compositional robot control that discovers a coherent style repertoire from diverse recordings and composes it with independent commands. First, motion retargeting maps the recordings to motions executable by the target robot; next, weakly supervised consensus encoding and density-based clustering identify styles within and across recordings without a prescribed count; finally, reinforcement learning trains a policy to compose the discovered styles with independent commands. We evaluate CODES on a Unitree Go2 quadruped across two simulators and physical hardware. Compared to baselines, CODES significantly improves kinematic coherence. Furthermore, our controller successfully tracks velocity commands that generalize beyond the support of the recorded data, exhibiting robust and distinguishable style characteristics during both cross-simulator and real-world hardware deployments.
  Project website: https://www.proroklab.org/compositional-motion-styles/

Robotics.title: ChairNav: Cross-Embodiment Pre-training and Personalization for Long-Horizon Wheelchair Navigation
Robotics.summary: Developing autonomous electric wheelchairs capable of long-horizon sidewalk navigation is critical for accessible personal mobility, yet existing approaches either focus on indoor map-based navigation or rely on expensive, complex sensor stacks to achieve full autonomy. In this work, we propose to tackle outdoor sidewalk navigation by leveraging visual navigation foundation models and large-scale navigation datasets, which offer strong generalization using lightweight hardware. To this end, we present ChairNav, a novel framework that adapts a general visual navigation model into a personalized electric wheelchair navigation system using a three-stage data pyramid. To address the scarcity of in-domain data, ChairNav first pre-trains on large-scale cross-embodiment datasets transformed into the wheelchair domain, followed by mid-training on a small number of wheelchair demonstrations to eliminate remaining domain gaps. Finally, a post-training stage refines the deployed model from user interventions to personalize its behavior. We deploy ChairNav on a commercial electric wheelchair equipped with an RGB-D camera and an onboard NVIDIA Jetson compute module. Experimental results validate the effectiveness of each stage in our data pyramid: pre-training reduces lateral ADE by 18%, and post-training increases the mean distance between user interventions from 29.2 m to 57.4 m. Further evaluation on kilometer-scale urban sidewalk routes shows that our system operates autonomously for 93.4% of total driving time, demonstrating its potential for everyday accessible mobility. Demo video and more details are at https://vail.cs.ucla.edu/ChairNav/.

Robotics.title: CLARO: Clutter Aware Robot Orchestrator for Open-Vocabulary Grasping using VLM Agents
Robotics.summary: Robots that follow natural-language instructions unlock a wide range of autonomous applications in households, warehouses, and labs. Real-world environments are diverse and often heavily cluttered, requiring robots to plan over multiple steps, act, and replan as they work toward a goal. We present CLARO (CLutter-Aware Robot Orchestrator), a VLM agent that orchestrates a set of perception and manipulation skills: open-vocabulary object detection, segmentation, 6-DoF grasping, and non-prehensile pushing to locate and retrieve a language-specified target in clutter. CLARO maintains a memory of its past actions to support long-horizon execution, and emits manipulation targets (grasp poses/3D waypoints) allowing transfer across robot arms without task-specific training.
