However, physical-state information can provide useful context for predicting how environments evolve. Prior work incorporates this information through different mechanisms: domain-specific physical laws can complicate multi-domain training, while supervision on individual frames or frame pairs gives limited attention to how physical state evolves over time. We introduce Time-JEPA, which fine-tunes a video world model using low-dimensional, temporally aligned physical time series as auxiliary supervision. Physical time series connect video representations with physical state at corresponding temporal positions, encouraging the model to preserve how physical state evolves. In multiple domains including autonomous driving, robot manipulation, and human motion, Time-JEPA improves current-state decoding, multi-horizon future-state prediction, and kinematic reconstruction over matched video-fine-tuned controls across both condition and state-variable distribution shifts. Multi-domain training provides aggregate gains over matched single-domain training in all three tasks. External evaluations further suggest that time-series supervision improves sensitivity to physical anomalies and the representation of physical interactions, including in unseen scenarios. Aggregate gains on a second video backbone indicate that the method can be applied to more backbones. These results suggest that physical time series help video world models better understand the physical world.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: RL Teaches VLMs Where to Attend but Not How to Perceive
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Although reinforcement learning (RL) effectively trains Vision-Language Model (VLM) agents, the mechanisms behind these capability gains are poorly understood. Across four diverse agent environments, we investigate whether the task-success gains from multi-turn RL are accompanied by improved grounded visual question answering about the environment. To assess this, we design environment-specific grounded VQA tasks that reveal improvements in grounded visual understanding. Representational probing shows that vision-encoder probe accuracy remains relatively stable, while LLM-layer probe accuracy improves. Attention analysis further reveals that LLM layers pay more attention to visual tokens during RL training. To test whether increased attention to visual tokens contributes to VQA gains, we introduce a lightweight plug-and-play intervention using a fixed attention bias. Without updating model parameters or computing gradients, this intervention partially restores VQA gains on the untrained model. These results reveal better utilization of visual information as a key mechanism behind the gains from RL.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Pretrained Features as Teachers, Not States: Compact Latent World Models for Visual Planning
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: A key design choice in visual world models is what information the latent state is encouraged to preserve. Models that learn a latent space with only a latent-prediction objective adapt to environment dynamics, but the predictive objective alone admits collapsed solutions and provides no explicit constraint on the visual information retained by the latent. Models built directly on pretrained visual features inherit a strong visual prior, but tie prediction and planning to a frozen state space. We propose Anchor-WM, which instead uses pretrained visual features as a teacher for learning a compact latent state rather than as the world-model state itself. Anchor-WM learns this compact latent with action-conditioned dynamics, while distilling the dense DINO representations through a training-only distillation head. This encourages the compact latent to retain visual information captured by the pretrained representation while discouraging representational collapse. At inference, the DINO encoder and distillation head are discarded, allowing prediction and planning to operate entirely in the learned latent space. Anchor-WM achieves the best average success rate across the four evaluated environments while enabling substantially faster planning than world models operating directly on DINO patch features. These results show that pretrained visual features can effectively guide world-model learning without defining the state space used for prediction and planning.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: BlenderWorld: Benchmarking Visual Agents for 3D Creation from Real-World References
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have enabled them to act as autonomous agents, creating and editing 3D models via code or direct software manipulation. In practical workflows, these models must infer object shapes, materials, spatial layouts, and lighting from diverse references while strictly following instructions to reconstruct, modify, or design 3D content. However, existing benchmarks provide limited coverage of such open-ended requests across real-world scenarios. To bridge this gap, we introduce BlenderWorld, the first comprehensive benchmark dedicated to evaluating frontier models on realistic 3D creation tasks. BlenderWorld comprises 223 tasks spanning architecture, products, natural environments, and scientific visualization, driven by text, image, video, and structured specification inputs. To rigorously assess these complex deliverables, we establish a unified evaluation protocol: we render the submitted Blender projects from multiple viewpoints and evaluate them against 2,651 task-specific binary rubrics alongside holistic visual quality scores. Benchmarking thirteen frontier models reveals that GPT-6-Astra achieves the highest overall fused score of 79.9, followed by Opus-5 (73.0) and GPT-5.6-Sol (67.7). Ultimately, our findings reveal a critical bottleneck: while current models can parse broad instructions, they still profoundly struggle with fine-grained 3D spatial coherence and accurate structural reproduction in Blender, leaving substantial headroom for future 3D-native agentics.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: What Generation Knows: Unlocking Fine-Grained Understanding in Unified Multimodal Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Fine-grained visual understanding requires distinguishing subtle differences in local attributes and spatial relations, yet remains challenging for existing vision-language models. Unified multimodal models (UMMs) offer a new opportunity through generation pathways that preserve rich visual information complementary to understanding. However, existing generation-assisted understanding methods mainly rely on generative supervision or explicit generation and have not systematically explored direct use of native generation-side representations. To address this gap, we systematically analyze what generation-side representations offer for fine-grained understanding, finding that they are more sensitive to fine-grained semantic changes, capture task-relevant changes missed by understanding-side representations, and depend on correct spatial organization for this advantage. Guided by these findings, we design GAFU, a post-training framework that unlocks native generation-side information for fine-grained understanding. It compresses generation-side visual representations into compact \(G\) tokens that preserve fine-grained visual details, enabling task-conditioned retrieval by the understanding pathway. Experiments show that GAFU consistently outperforms SFT baselines trained on the same data across diverse visual understanding tasks and UMM architectures, with maximum relative improvements of 20.00\%, 17.94\%, and 8.62\% on VStar-Bench, OmniSpatial, and VSR-Bench, respectively. Overall, GAFU converts complementary information from the generation pathway into gains in fine-grained visual understanding, providing an effective path toward synergy between generation and understanding in UMMs.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Single-Pass Decision Scores Enable Rapid Classification with Adjustable Thresholds in Medical Multimodal Large Language Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) answer binary clinical questions with a yes or no token, leaving the decision threshold implicit and fixed. We derive a continuous score from a single forward pass by renormalizing the probabilities of the yes and no tokens, allowing the threshold to be adapted to clinical needs without retraining. We evaluated this approach with MedGemma and Gemma-3 (4B and 27B) on six medical imaging datasets. The default threshold was frequently misaligned with the task: for identifying normal chest radiographs, MedGemma-27B labeled every image as abnormal, whereas a validation-selected threshold yielded a sensitivity of 0.945 and a specificity of 0.696. Normalization achieved the highest AUROC on four of six datasets (CheXpert: 0.819 vs. 0.777 for raw and 0.743 for text-elicited probabilities), and a single decision required 53-79 ms on one GPU. This simple post-hoc method turns medical MLLMs into fast classifiers with adjustable operating points. Code: https://github.com/TruhnLab/llm-threshold-calibration

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Automatic Cause Determination in Road Scene Understanding Using Qualitative Reasoning and Four-Valued Logic
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Road scene understanding in automated driving (AD) aims to build a comprehensive analysis of video sequences taken on the road by embedded or fixed cameras (e.g., mounted on vertical road signals). One goal is to identify the relevant actors in the scene and another goal is to determine the causes that have triggered a specific action of the ego car (i.e., stop, slow down, turn left, etc.). In a complex urban environment, these causes can be multiple, confusing, possibly contradictory to other causes and not easily expressible using simplistic reasoning. Still, providing accurate {\it automatic cause determination} supports a) user acceptance by providing appropriate explanations to the car passengers and road users; b) increased road safety by providing detailed road scene understanding to traffic. In this paper, we propose using spatiotemporal reasoning and Belnap's four-valued logic to formulate complex causes of AD action in a road scene. We compute these causes by analysing a Qualitative eXplainable Graph (QXG), which is an abstract representation of the road scene capturing spatiotemporal relations between road entities. Starting from a QXG, our approach called \tool, is targeted to determine complex causes of a selected AD action occurring in a specific frame of a road scene. The usefulness of \tool is demonstrated on several scenes extracted from the well-known NuScene dataset.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: 2025 IEEE Intelligent Vehicles Symposium (IV), pp. 1056-1061 (2025)

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: ProV-Mem: Proactive Memory for Streaming Video Question Answering
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Proactive streaming video question answering requires a model to continuously monitor an incoming stream and autonomously decide when to speak, what to say, and whether to emit a response. Existing streaming systems face a fundamental difficulty: retaining long visual histories is costly, whereas discarding them can lead to missed events and repeated responses. We propose \textbf{ProV-Mem}, a training-free proactive memory framework built around a frozen VLM backbone. ProV-Mem decomposes the proactive decision into three lightweight memory tiers: a temporal-trigger memory controls when to query the backbone and recovers from prolonged silence, an instructional memory guides what to say through a fixed prompting prior for concise and visually grounded generation, and an episodic memory determines whether to emit by filtering near-duplicate responses. Under an idealized conditional-sufficiency assumption, we derive a stagewise approximation bound relating the decomposed process to a full-state joint policy. We further introduce Cost-Aware Area Under the Curve (\textbf{CAUC}), which extends PAUC by explicitly discounting redundant, overly frequent, and unnecessarily long emissions. Experiments on the four scenarios of ProactiveVideoQA show that ProV-Mem achieves the best CAUC across all scenarios and the best PAUC on WEB, EGO, and TV, while maintaining low per-response inference latency.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Causal Spatio-Temporal Neural Distance Fields for Counterfactual Cardiac Anatomy
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Counterfactual cardiac anatomy can support risk modelling and intervention planning, by predicting how a patient's heart would change under altered clinical conditions. However, current shape generative models are conditional on clinical variables and disregard causal links between these variables. Thus, they cannot answer counterfactual questions about how a given subject's anatomy would change under a different clinical profile. Modelling the heart's continuous movement over the cardiac cycle requires a representation that is itself continuous in space and time. Spatio-temporal neural distance fields provide this while separating clinical conditioning from subject-specific shape. We place a structural causal model (SCM) over the set of clinical variables (age, sex, smoking, BMI, heart rate, systolic blood pressure), before the condition encoding of the spatio-temporal neural distance field which represents the left atrial complex over a cardiac cycle by signed distance fields. An intervention of the clinical variables, propagated through a SCM before the 4D counterfactual, is constructed from the neural distance field. The generated counterfactuals follow dose-response under age interventions and transforms the male distribution to closely match the female distribution under the intervention $\mathrm{do(\mathrm{female}{=}1)}$. By doing inverse interventions the model also approximates the original anatomy with sub millimeter precision. To our knowledge, this is the first counterfactual generation of 4D cardiac anatomy and the first integration of an SCM with an implicit neural representation as its imaging mechanism.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: spora: A Unified Multimodal Dataset and Platform for Spatial Proteomics
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Spatial proteomics (SP) captures the molecular composition and spatial organization of tissues at single-cell resolution, opening a direct view of the cellular ecosystems that drive disease. Protein panels, acquisition platforms, and tissue contexts differ from one cohort to the next, and a coherent picture of tissue biology can only emerge from models trained to bridge this heterogeneity. Foundation models offer the natural path forward, but their training depends on large, harmonized corpora that span platforms, panels, and cohorts. No public resource currently approaches that scale; available data sit in small, narrowly scoped releases with incompatible formats and conventions. We present $\texttt{spora}$, a large-scale multimodal SP dataset of 13,546 standardized multiplex images from 5,477 patients across 35 cohorts and five major SP technologies. Curated with biomedical experts, $\texttt{spora}$ provides model training-ready formats together with cell and tissue segmentations, structured clinical metadata, and, where available, paired H&E enabling the training of virtual staining models. It is complemented by $\texttt{spora [io]}$, a unified interface for tiling, sampling, and standardization across all cohorts and modalities, and $\texttt{spora [bench]}$, a benchmark suite spanning cell phenotyping, diagnostic and therapeutic prediction as well as virtual staining tasks across twelve cohorts that places current SP foundation models on common ground against task specific baselines.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: PACE: Pareto-Adaptive Compression for Efficient Native MLLMs
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Native multimodal large language models (native MLLMs) jointly encode visual and linguistic sequences within a unified autoregressive Transformer, emerging as a promising paradigm for multimodal understanding. Unlike conventional ViT-based MLLMs relying on external vision encoders, ViT-free native MLLMs tokenize pixel patches directly, potentially suffering severe visual token redundancy. A pilot study confirms this: unlike ViT-based models that degrade under compression, ViT-free MLLMs tolerate aggressive compression with near-lossless or even improved performance. Yet existing compression methods target ViT-based settings, leaving native MLLMs, which stand to gain the most, unexplored. To close this gap, we introduce an analysis pipeline centered on token discriminability and cross-dimensional heterogeneous redundancy, revealing that (i) redundancy is distributed independently and heterogeneously along height and width axes, and (ii) early-layer visual tokens are indiscriminable and uniformly redundant. Guided by these findings, we propose PACE (Pareto-Adaptive Compression for Efficient Native MLLMs), the first visual token compression framework tailored for native MLLMs with Multimodal-RoPE. Leveraging dimensional decoupling of positional encoding, PACE decomposes attention into two orthogonal spatial saliency estimates along height and width, gated by a positional attention signal, yielding direction-aware importance with negligible overhead. It further casts token budget allocation as Pareto optimization over performance preservation, inference efficiency, and spatial coverage, jointly identifying optimal compression depths and retention ratios. Experiments show PACE maintains near-lossless performance at only 25%-50% visual token retention, even improving several benchmarks, while delivering over 2x FLOPs reduction.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: SynerGest: Temporal-Spatial Synergistic Gesture Generation for Dyadic Conversations
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Co-speech gesture generation in dyadic conversations for creating immersive virtual avatars remains highly challenging. Existing models often struggle to balance kinematic stability with rhythmic responsiveness and suffer from semantic entanglement, leading to either generic mean-pose regression or unnatural micro-jitters. To address these challenges, we propose SynerGest, a high-fidelity dyadic gesture generation framework grounded in Contrastive Flow Matching (CFM). Specifically, our CFM objective explicitly penalizes mismatched semantic pairs during training, discouraging spatial shortcuts and over-smoothed predictions while improving conditional semantic alignment. Furthermore, to overcome architectural bottlenecks, we introduce the Impulse-Trend Synergistic Attention (ITSA) module. Grounded in the key insight of decoupling "what moves" from "when it moves," ITSA models sharp, speech-driven rhythmic impulses separately from continuous kinematic trends, supporting precise audio-motion synchronization and global structural stability. Extensive qualitative and quantitative evaluations on two public datasets demonstrate that SynerGest achieves state-of-the-art performance, delivering contextually responsive and kinematically fluid dyadic interactions.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Generative Text Modelling and Language-Guided Visual Attention for Deciphering Palimpsests
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Recovering obscured text in palimpsests, i.e. the manuscripts where the original writing (under-text) was erased and overwritten for reuse, is vital for preserving lost information. Due to the nature of the material, such a task can be highly challenging and time-consuming. This paper presents an approach towards automated palimpsest handwritten text modeling for under-text recovery. We investigate generative models, including Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and diffusion models, and design a custom denoising diffusion model that learns structured noise patterns to reconstruct the under-text. The recovered text is subsequently processed by a fine-tuned, attention-based handwritten text recognition network. Furthermore, we investigate a language-guided recognition framework that leverages textual class descriptions as informative priors, enabling the text recognition model to distinguish meaningful features from noise. This is achieved by grounding task-specific descriptions, phrased in words or sentences, through visual attention maps generated by pretrained vision-language models like CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training). To facilitate future research and benchmarking, we release new datasets for synthetic palimpsests (currently scarce), CLIP-compatible text descriptions, and pre-trained models with code.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: OrTeN: Neural Inverse Graphics for Joint Terrain and Line-scan Camera Trajectory Reconstruction
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Digital terrain maps (DTMs) are used for landing site selection, terrain-relative navigation, and geological analysis in planetary exploration. Existing state-of-practice reconstruction techniques for creating DTMs from satellite imagery use multi-view stereo, requiring complex pipelines for dealing with camera error, changing illumination, and images with limited disparity. This work introduces Orbital Terrain Networks (OrTeN), a DTM construction method that uses neural inverse rendering to jointly optimize a textured height map and orbital camera corrections from line-scan satellite images. OrTeN operates directly on calibrated line-scan images with pixel values expressed as radiance factor (I/F) and corrects both broad trajectory pose inconsistencies and high-frequency pointing jitter jointly with surface reconstruction during training. Surface-projected patch normalized cross-correlation (NCC) enforces consistency between observations of the same terrain, refining an initial rough reconstruction. A semi-empirical reflectance model and shadow rendering are used to fit surface appearance from multi-date imagery with differing solar illumination. OrTeN requires only calibrated line-scan images and initial camera poses and does not use any structural priors including ranging/depth measurements or initial rough DTMs. OrTeN is evaluated on four planetary imagery datasets. Aligned terrain RMSEs are 2.35 m at Jezero Crater, 2.82 m at Gale Crater, 16.18 m at Olympus Mons, and 0.43 m at McGetchin Crater.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: BiNar: Bitstream Native Restorer for Bitstream-corrupted Image Restoration
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Bitstream-corrupted image restoration (BCIR) aims to reconstruct faithful images from corrupted compressed bitstreams. However, corruption occurs in bitstream-domain may lead to unpredictable error propagation and distortion amplification in pixel-domain, and even result in complete undecodability by standard decoders, posing significant challenge to existing image restoration paradigms. To address this challenge, we propose Bitstream Native Restorer (BiNar), a generative restoration framework that leverages fine-grained bitstream-native semantics to guide bitstream-corrupted image restoration. In BiNar, Bitstream Semantic Modeling (BSeM) extracts robust informative semantics and models sequential bytes directly from corrupted bitstream, enabling to generate fine-grained bitstream descriptions without relying on pixel decoding. Based on the descriptions,the Corruption-adaptive Multimodal Semantic Aggregation (CMSA) further extracts adaptive visual modal cues in decoded corrupted images and aggregates to bitstream descriptions. The multimodal aggregated fine-grained descriptions can serve as coherent restoration guidance. Finally, Blind Corruption Localization (BCoL) exploits the segmentation prior of visual foundation models to identify and locate error regions that requires recovery in corrupted images. The located error regions and the fine-grained descriptions jointly serve as visual prompt and language prompt of diffusion models image restoration, respectively. Extensive experiments under diverse bitstream corruption conditions show that BiNar outperforms all State-of-the-arts image restoration models regardless of perceptual quality or objective quality. Ablation studies demonstrate the effectiveness of fine-grained bitstream-native semantics in BCIR task.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Hierarchical and Query-Aware Visual Token Pruning for High-Resolution LVLMs
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: High-resolution Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) preserve critical, fine-grained visual details by encoding a global thumbnail alongside multiple local crops. However, the resulting thousands of vision tokens introduce severe computational bottlenecks during Large Language Model (LLM) inference. Existing token pruning methods rely primarily on query-agnostic visual saliency, while current query-aware approaches either operate at a coarse crop-level resolution or compute token relevance too late, after vision tokens have already entered the heavy LLM layers. To address this, we propose a training-free, hierarchical token pruning framework that utilizes query guidance prior to executing any LLM blocks. Our top-down hierarchy first operates at the instance-level, dynamically scaling the vision token retention ratio of each sample based on its visual complexity. Next, at the crop-level, we distribute this sample budget across local crops using sentence-level cross-modal similarity. Finally, at the token-level, we exploit projected vision tokens alongside textual query token embeddings in the shared space to measure fine-grained alignment, applying a text-debiasing normalization to produce high-fidelity query scores. These query-guided budgets and scores are fused with local and global visual saliency metrics to select the most critical vision tokens. Extensive experiments on LLaVA-NeXT-7B demonstrate that our plug-and-play framework retains 98.0% and 94.8% of unpruned performance at 25% and 10% vision token retention, respectively. Notably, at 25% retention, our method delivers a 2.0x inference throughput speedup and even surpasses the unpruned baseline on POPE by 0.7 points.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: BLANC: Adaptive Temporal Scheduling for Sign Language Production
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Sign language production (SLP) aims to synthesize expressive signing motion from written text. Modeling signing motion presents two key temporal challenges. First, fine-grained hand articulations demand higher temporal resolution than relatively slower body movements. Second, signing events unfold over variable durations, calling for adaptive temporal scheduling during generation. To address these challenges, we first introduce a Multi-Rate Vector Quantizer (MRVQ), an articulation-decoupled motion tokenizer that represents the body and both hands as separate discrete streams at distinct temporal resolutions. Building on this representation, we propose BLANC (BLock-wise Adaptive diffusioN with Articulatory Clock), a gloss-free SLP framework that generates variable-duration motion blocks causally while denoising tokens in parallel within each block. At its core, a Latent Articulatory Clock (LAC) learns temporal structure from multi-scale motion-derived partitions to predict block durations and sequence termination during generation. We further introduce inference-time body-conditioned hand refinement to improve coordination across articulators. Extensive experiments on PHOENIX-2014T and CSL-Daily demonstrate that BLANC achieves state-of-the-art performance in sign language production.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: HAVANA: A Hierarchical Video-Action Model for Vision-Language Navigation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) requires long-horizon instruction-consistent planning and short-horizon local planning in current geometry. Video-action models (VAMs) offer a promising way to learn predictive representations for navigation. However, existing VAMs jointly predict visual futures and local trajectories in a single process, even though they operate at different paces: future prediction remains stable across multiple updates while local trajectories must react to fresh observations. To bridge this gap, we introduce HAVANA, a dual-system VAM that decouples predictive reasoning from reactive local planning. A slow system produces a compact language-conditioned latent plan from observation history, while a fast system combines the latest plan with the current observation to generate local trajectories. Their asynchronous execution enables rapid adaptation without repeated future prediction, and no future video is generated during inference. Experiments on OmniNavBench demonstrate state-of-the-art navigation performance over prior baselines, while real-world deployments further show robust generalization to unseen environments across different robot embodiments. Our code and checkpoints will be available at https://github.com/Anastasiawd/HAVANA.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: NV-Generate-Body: 3D Latent Diffusion Model forControllable Anatomy, Tumor, and Demographic Body Mask Synthesis
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Curating large labeled CT datasets is expensive and constrained by patient privacy. We present NV-Generate-BodyMask, a 3D latent diffusion model that synthesizes whole-body CT segmentation masks with precise, joint control over organ anatomy, tumor burden, and patient demographics. The model operates in the compressed latent space of a frozen mask autoencoder, generating $256^3$ volumetric label maps conditioned on a 19-dimensional vector via Adaptive Group Normalization and cross-attention. A size-adaptive ROI loss with spatial halo weighting and a paired tumor injection pipeline enable accurate tumor size conditioning despite the scarcity of annotated tumor cases. Trained on 8,571 masks across 26 cohorts spanning 132 labels, the model achieves Spearman $\rho = 0.70$--$0.92$ for organ size, 85--100\% tumor recall for lung, pancreatic, colon, and bone lesions, and strong demographic alignment (BMI $\rho = 0.78$, sex-conditioned perfect prostate control).

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: SERO: Semantic Prediction for Single-Step Object Removal
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Object removal and semantic inpainting of missing regions remain inherently ill-posed, as multiple plausible completions may exist for a given scene. Recent diffusion-based methods have demonstrated strong potential for high-quality object removal; however, they still face two key limitations. First, although they can synthesise sharp and high-resolution images, they often struggle to complete removed regions in a semantically consistent and contextually meaningful manner, where the generated content should agree with the surrounding scene layout and object relationships rather than merely appear visually realistic. Second, their iterative denoising process makes them computationally expensive, limiting their practicality for downstream applications. We propose SERO, a semantic prediction framework for single-step object removal. Our model predicts a hidden-region semantic prior in embedding space, which guides a latent bridge-matching generator toward plausible scene completion by providing both where to edit and what structure is likely to exist behind the removed object. This enables visually realistic and contextually coherent completions in one forward pass. Experiments on the RORD and OBER datasets show that SERO achieves competitive or state-of-the-art performance while requiring only a single generation step.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Precision Cotton Disease Management: Leveraging UAV Imagery and Custom YOLO Deep Learning Framework for Enhanced Detection
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Cotton sustains the textile economies of over 80 countries with an annual yield of 113 million bales, yet 30-60% of yield losses are still attributed to viral, bacterial, and fungal diseases that remain undetected until manual field scouting. To address this critical issue, the integration of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) imagery with deep learning offers a scalable early-warning system; however, existing models suffer from low early-stage accuracy, poor transferability, and high computational cost. In this paper, we propose Cotton-Vision, a fully convolutional single-stage detector that synergizes three lightweight architectural innovations: Ghost Bottleneck modules for a 20% parameter reduction, Efficient Channel Attention (ECA) for adaptive feature recalibration, and Cross-Stage Partial (CSP) fusion for enriched gradient flow. The network is trained on a novel dataset collected across seven cotton fields in the Punjab province of Pakistan, comprising over 2,700 high-resolution drone images. Extensive data augmentation (rotation, shear, exposure, and saturation) expands the dataset to 11,704 training samples. On a held-out test set, Cotton-Vision achieves a precision of 97.7%, a recall of 77.7%, an mAP@50 of 85.6%, and an mAP@50-95 of 76.6%. These results represent a 10-20% improvement in precision, recall, and mAP over state-of-the-art baselines, including YOLOv5, YOLOv8, YOLOv11, YOLOv12, RT-DETR, and RF-DETR. Through a comprehensive ablation study, we demonstrate that each proposed architectural enhancement contributes to the model's superior performance, yielding a 12-16% mAP improvement over the baseline architecture. Our findings confirm that this synergy of lightweight and attention-based modules provides a robust, computationally viable solution for early cotton disease detection.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: PREEMPT: Proactive Robustness Evaluation under Editing for Media Protection Techniques
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Proactive image protection methods aim to defend visual content against unauthorized manipulation and generative misuse by embedding protective signals into images before release. Evaluating whether these protections remain effective under image editing is therefore critical. However, existing evaluations remain largely limited to one-shot edits, providing only a static view of robustness while overlooking its evolution under realistic multi-step editing workflows. To systematically characterize robustness dynamics under sequential editing across various protection paradigms, we introduce PREEMPT, a holistic evaluation framework. It evaluates protection robustness under both one-shot and sequential editing scenarios, covering image transformations, semantic edits, homogeneous and heterogeneous edit compositions. To enable consistent analysis across protection paradigms with different underlying objectives, PREEMPT normalizes task-specific effectiveness into protection survival trajectories and summarizes long-horizon robustness through trajectory-based diagnostics. Using this framework, we reveal that degradation behaviors remain hidden under conventional one-shot evaluation. Furthermore, perturbation- and watermark-based protection methods exhibit different failure modes, and the first semantic edit largely determines subsequent degradation trajectories. PREEMPT provides a standardized protocol for studying long-horizon robustness and offers new insights into the degradation dynamics of proactive image protection.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Landmark-Free and Scale-Blind Multi-View Registration of Preoperative Liver Models to Intraoperative Surfaces
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Augmented-reality guidance in laparoscopic liver resection requires aligning preoperative 3D liver models from CT/MRI with intraoperative surfaces. Monocular reconstruction in most cases cannot guarantee scale, albeit rigid-motion registration requires scale as an input. Our proposed framework ``SimCompose'' estimates the full similarity transformation $\Sim$, including scale, without relying on landmarks and applies the same transformation across multiple views with known relative geometry. However, reliable detection of registration failures remains challenging in surgical settings, where ground-truth alignment is generally unavailable. For this, we propose a geometry-based selector that evaluates candidate transformations without requiring ground truth. Large disagreement among these transformations is used to flag potentially unreliable registrations. Finally, we propose to use a non-rigid refinement based on a low-dimensional deformation model from Neo-Hookean simulations in the Simulation Open Framework Architecture (SOFA), without additional network training. SimCompose is trained exclusively on synthetic partial views. Its encoder processes point clouds normalised to a unit root-mean-square radius, without access to metric scale, and filters each view before multi-view fusion. Evaluation on unseen synthetic data (300 single-view pairs per run; 100 three-view registrations) shows that multi-view integration and candidate selection increase the success rate under stringent $\Sim$ accuracy criteria from 38.4% for a single-view, single-method configuration to 77%. Existing learning-based baselines do not satisfy these criteria even when provided with the exact scale. On five in-vivo patients with 92 keyframes, the rigid registration stage reduces surface error more than three-fold relative to learning-based baselines with external scale information.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Ghost Attack: Using 19th-Century Illusions to Fool 21st-Century Biometrics
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: While the Pepper's Ghost illusion is a 19th-century optical technique, we found that this forgotten gimmick exposes vulnerabilities in modern face recognition systems. This paper introduces the 'Ghost Attack': a physical attack that repurposes this classic illusion using low-cost, free-space hardware and a transparent medium to project high-resolution facial data into physical 3D space. We show in the paper that despite relying on centuries-old optical principles, this new attack type simultaneously breaks three components of modern facial recognition systems (FRS): (a) the face matcher, (b) the presentation attack detection module, and (c) the morphing attack detection component, resulting in high impersonation success rates against state-of-the-art algorithms without triggering presentation or morphing defenses. These findings reveal a significant blind spot in current biometric systems, which fail to account for transparent projections and evolving physical attack vectors. To support further research, we are offering the dataset of face images of 100 identities, re-captured with and without 'ghost' projections as a new benchmark representing a novel attack for face recognition.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: ULIFLOW: Unified Latent Human-Object Interaction Flow
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Text-conditioned 3D human--object interaction (HOI) generation remains challenging because individually plausible human and object motions do not necessarily form a coherent interaction. We argue that a key limitation lies in conventional skeleton-based representations, which compactly describe body kinematics while leaving surface-level interaction geometry largely implicit, often requiring additional contact-specific regularizers. We propose ULIFlow, a framework that explicitly models continuous human--object relations within a unified latent space. To this end, we derive continuous marker--object relations from sparse body-surface markers and treat them as an explicit interaction modality alongside human motion and object dynamics. A Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) autoencoder is then designed to jointly model these heterogeneous streams while preserving their modality-specific structures. Importantly, we let the relation stream directly participate in human and object reconstruction, encouraging the shared latent representation to preserve both individual dynamics and the interaction geometry that coordinates them. To further achieve variable-length generation, we introduce a blockwise Flow Forcing scheme with global sequence-progress conditioning, enabling progressive continuation from fixed-length training windows while maintaining consistent long-horizon dynamics. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ULIFlow consistently outperforms prior work in overall generation quality and human--object coordination, while preserving coherent interactions over requested durations beyond the training horizon.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: CRISP: Progressive Illumination Curriculum for Recurrent Low-Light Video Enhancement with Semantic Priors
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Low-light video enhancement requires the recovery of brightness, color, and fine spatial structures while preserving temporal coherence in the presence of noise and motion. Existing methods often struggle to balance these objectives, particularly in severely degraded regions. This paper presents CRISP, a recurrent framework trained using a progressive illumination curriculum. Its two-frame recurrent architecture propagates information across successive frames to exploit temporal context beyond the immediate input pair. During training, supervision progressively transitions from intermediate targets interpolated between the low-light input and the reference to the full reference, gradually increasing the required brightness and color correction. This curriculum stabilizes recurrent training without introducing additional inference cost and yields the largest performance improvement among the components evaluated in the ablation study. To further support structural reconstruction, the framework optionally incorporates frozen DINOv3 semantic features through adaptive layer normalization (AdaLN)-style modulation, without fine-tuning the foundation model. Experiments on DID and BVI-RLV demonstrate that CRISP achieves the highest PSNR on DID and the highest SSIM on BVI-RLV among the evaluated methods, while maintaining computational efficiency.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Hexagonal Basis Projectors for Model-Based Iterative CT Reconstruction
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Image representation affects both the forward model and quantitative feature recovery in model-based iterative CT reconstruction. For isotropically bandlimited signals, the hexagonal lattice is the most sampling-efficient lattice in two dimensions, with greater directional isotropy and a larger alias-free bandwidth than the Cartesian grid at equal density. We develop constant and linear hexagonal projectors for two-dimensional fan-beam CT using box spline calculus. Both bases form a partition of unity on common coefficient centers; the linear tent also reproduces affine functions. We derive analytic ray footprints and effective detector-blur expressions and implement efficient GPU forward and backprojection. On simulated FORBILD data, the linear model improves on Cartesian and hexagonal pixels, with its best noisy-data accuracy at the coarser resolution. Real-world 2DeteCT comparisons use high-dose, high-resolution Cartesian reconstructions as pseudo ground truth and show competitive image and feature agreement. These results establish a practical hexagonal representation for quantitative CT.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: PACE-Mem: Prefix-Aware Complementary Evidence for Multimodal Agents
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: As multimodal agents accumulate experience, their long-term memories contain many similar observations of recurring scenes, actions, and entities. Answer quality depends on the evidence retrieved from these memories into the model's context. However, query-relevant memories may contain overlapping information, and a fixed retrieval depth may return too little or too much evidence for a given question. To address these challenges, we propose PACE-Mem, Prefix-Aware Complementary Evidence, which constructs a complementary evidence sequence and determines its length from the same selection trajectory. For structured memories, query-guided pooling combines records within each clip to obtain relevance scores and representations. Using these relevance scores and representations, maximal marginal relevance (MMR) selection balances query relevance against overlap with previously selected evidence. From the resulting score trajectory, a prefix-length selection algorithm determines retrieval depth by comparing length-normalized adjacent declines, accounting for both score changes and the amount of evidence accumulated. PACE-Mem is a training-free, plug-in retrieval method for clip-based agent memory systems, leaving memory construction and answer generation unchanged. Across three long-video benchmarks and two agent frameworks, PACE-Mem improves question-answering accuracy by an average of 1.6% over Adaptive-k, the strongest baseline at comparable mean retrieval depths. Further analysis reveals that jointly adding and removing evidence is associated with larger net accuracy gains than either change alone.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Learning from the Right Regions: Class-Conditioned Explanation Guidance for Medical Imaging
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Deep neural networks can achieve strong predictive performance in medical imaging while relying on regions unrelated to the predicted finding. Explanation-guided learning can address this problem, but multi-label classification introduces a key challenge: multiple abnormalities may coexist in an image, requiring each prediction to align with its corresponding spatial evidence. We propose a class-conditioned explanation-guided learning framework that constructs a separate explanation for each positive class and penalizes evidence outside its class-specific annotated regions. We instantiate the framework using Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) and evaluate it on 14 abnormalities using EfficientNet-B1, ViT-B/16, ViT-B/32, and Swin-B. Explanation guidance substantially improves annotation alignment across all architectures: All-Saliency Precision increases from 0.140 to 0.625, 0.052 to 0.551, 0.060 to 0.403, and 0.095 to 0.570, respectively. These improvements are accompanied by smaller, architecture-dependent changes in classification performance. Our results show that class-conditioned explanation guidance can substantially improve where multi-label classifiers concentrate their explanatory evidence while largely preserving predictive performance.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Spatons: Spatiotonally Localized Building Blocks for Efficient XR Predistortion
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: We present Spatons, a family of compositional, spatially localized neural operators for computationally efficient XR (extended reality) predistortion and distortion compensation. XR displays (AR, VR, and MR) suffer from spatial (e.g., geometric) and tonal (e.g., colour) distortions. Frames can be pre-distorted so that the projected image looks as intended. Distortions vary with manufacturing tolerances and projection systems, motivating programmable compensation. Untethered, battery-operated XR systems also require low energy and latency. A Spaton is a hybrid patch-to-pixel block combining tiny Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLPs) with fixed-function interpolation. Using Spatons, we build programmable, computationally efficient pipelines for varied distortion scenarios. On the full spatiotonal Scenario 5, Sequential-5' matches CompenNet++ in SSIM (0.944 vs. 0.944) and closely matches its PSNR (27.5 vs. 27.7 dB), with substantially lower complexity. We demonstrate a flexible Spaton solution with 6 times fewer FLOPs and 106 times fewer parameters than CompenNet++, and 4-10 times fewer memory transfers than UNet++. We characterize software implementations and analytical hardware estimates, including optimizations across target XR platforms. The distortions considered are drawn mostly from see-through, near-eye displays, where the spatial light path governs local intensity and spectral response. This early systems-level exploration uses closed-form differentiable distortions and one real projector-camera capture set for training and evaluation, rather than through-the-optics measurements. Testing on a wider range of real XR devices remains future work. Chromatic dispersion (color fringes) remains the main artifact where Spatons trail monolithic baselines.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: ZeroDSS: Semantic Segmentation from Class Names Alone
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Semantic segmentation depends heavily on real images with pixel-level annotations, making dense supervision a major obstacle to deployment in new domains. We study task-specific data-free semantic segmentation, where training uses generic pretrained generative priors but has access to no target-domain images, masks, or captions--only a predefined category set. We introduce Zero-Data Semantic Segmentation (ZeroDSS), a feedback-driven approach that treats synthetic supervision as an adaptively controllable training distribution rather than a direct surrogate for real data. ZeroDSS constructs a semantically structured prompt distribution through LLM-guided compositional generation and adaptive class rebalancing, then converts the prompts into image-mask pairs using diffusion attention. Its feedback-driven distribution refinement consists of a two-phase closed-loop training procedure with a single loop-back step. In Phase I, a segmenter is trained using confidence-weighted supervision and dual-scale consistency. In Phase II, model feedback is used to adaptively target underperforming categories and refine diffusion-derived masks using model predictions. After this refined initial training, a teacher-student framework is utilized in the final phase to iteratively improve the fused supervision and segmenter through exponential moving average (EMA) updates. Using synthetic training data only, ZeroDSS achieves 35.0% mIoU on MS COCO with DeepLabV3, and 66.3% and 63.5% mIoU on PASCAL VOC with DeepLabV3 and Mask2Former, respectively. These results show that explicitly constructing and iteratively refining the synthetic supervision distribution can substantially reduce the synthetic-to-real gap in dense prediction.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: S3D-Mosaic: Subgradient-Guided Cross-Band Structure Transfer for Spectral Demosaicing
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Multispectral filter array (MSFA) imaging enables snapshot spectral acquisition, but its per-band sparse sampling causes severe spatial aliasing. Although missing spatial structures can be inferred across bands, wavelength-dependent contrast variations make direct cross-band transfer unreliable. Existing model-based methods lack explicit magnitude-invariant mechanisms, and learning-based methods require layout-specific training or per-image tuning, limiting generalization. To address these issues, we propose S3D-Mosaic, a model-based spectral demosaicing method built upon a subgradient-guided cross-band structure transfer framework. We first establish a subgradient-guided regularization framework with a generalized cosine-similarity interpretation, providing a convex mechanism for magnitude-invariant information transfer. Then we design a compact Directional Sparse Equivariant Difference Convolution (DSE-DConv) for band-level extraction of orientation-selective, high-frequency structure features at low computational cost. Instantiating the framework with DSE-DConv on spectrally adjacent bands yields a cross-band self-structure similarity regularizer for spectral demosaicing, which we optimize via a dual-scan ADMM algorithm that decouples the bidirectional dependency while propagating magnitude-robust structural information across bands. With DSE-DConv's two parameters trained once via self-supervision, S3D-Mosaic outperforms state-of-the-art unsupervised methods on CAVE and NTIRE 2022, and generalizes robustly to varying MSFA layouts, pan-mosaic fusion, and real-world UAV data with fixed reconstruction hyperparameters. The source code is available at \url{https://github.com/bestwishes43/S3D-Mosaic}.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: BodyBridge: Grounded Body Layers for Sim-to-Real Translation of Vulnerable Road Users
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Simulation-to-real driving video diffusion models can translate photorealistic scenes, but they typically represent pedestrians and cyclists, vulnerable road users (VRUs), as generic object classes. This is insufficient for vulnerable road users whose safety-relevant appearance depends on articulated pose and identity. We present BodyBridge and Grounded Body Layers (GBL), a simulator-derived, pixel-aligned representation that combines scene geometry, canonical per-pixel body correspondence, and exact VRU masks. GBL provides explicit articulation to the video diffusion model, emphasizes VRU regions during control-branch post-training, and supports additive composition with scene-geometry control at inference. It also enables per-joint evaluation of generated VRUs and a failure taxonomy for identity errors. On CARLA-to-real translation, BodyBridge improves near-range PCK@0.5 by 22% over the released depth-conditioned baseline. Replacing normal-map body control with canonical correspondence reduces body flips by 18%, while composition reduces near-range facing flips by 27%. These results show that explicit body grounding complements scene-level control and improves pose-faithful VRU generation. All code, data, and model checkpoints will be made publicly available to support reproducible, pedestrian-aware autonomous driving research.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Do 3D Large Language Models Really Use 3D Evidence?
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Recent 3D Large Language Models (3D-LLMs) have shown strong performance on scene question answering with extensive post-training. Yet, existing benchmarks rarely evaluate how 3D-LLMs respond to referential ambiguity, insufficient scene evidence, or false presuppositions, obscuring whether their responses are grounded in 3D evidence. In this work, we introduce UNICORNS, a benchmark for evaluating the reliability of 3D-LLM responses across four evidence conditions. UNICORNS contains 11,387 questions across 557 ScanNet scans, covering eight challenge categories alongside answerable controls. A response passes only if it satisfies the required response behavior and contains no scene claim unsupported by the available evidence. Evaluation of six open-sourced 3D-LLMs reveals a pronounced performance gap: even the strongest zero-shot model achieves 61.22% accuracy on answerable controls, but only 40.94% across the eight challenge categories. To address this gap, we further propose HORN, an obligation-aware post-training method combining group-relative task rewards, leaf-conditioned obligation rewards, and supervised control replay. Extensive experiments demonstrate that HORN reaches $75.1 \pm 1.0\%$ across the challenge categories and $77.2 \pm 0.8\%$ overall, outperforming all baselines without degrading answerable-control accuracy. Our findings enable a systematic evaluation and improvement of evidence-grounded 3D reasoning for 3D-LLMs (code: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/unicorns-6B38/).

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: HumanSkill-4D: Training-Free Language Querying of Animatable Gaussian Avatars in Space and Time
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: We introduce avatar referring segmentation, which selects regions of animatable Gaussian avatars from language queries. A query can also specify a pose or motion to select matching intervals. This lets users interact with avatars for local editing and motion inspection. However, making these selections with existing language Gaussian splatting methods poses two challenges: adjacent parts and garments are hard to separate and may be referred to indirectly (region ambiguity), while fine-grained motions can look alike in RGB (motion ambiguity). We address these challenges with HumanSkill-4D, a training-free framework that shares a multimodal large language model (MLLM) and geometric operators across avatars. For each avatar, a semantic memory links body-part and garment categories to persistent Gaussian regions and appearance descriptions. The MLLM uses category names and descriptions to select categories by appearance, relation, or function. To find matching intervals, it composes operators into programs that check query conditions on driving joint trajectories stored in a motion memory. These category choices and operator outputs make selections traceable, while composing or adding operators supports new motion conditions. To evaluate this task, we introduce three human-annotated benchmarks and show that HumanSkill-4D outperforms the baselines in part segmentation and 3D and 4D referring segmentation, with compact memories and only minutes of setup per avatar.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: O-SCD++: Replay-Free Online Scene Change Detection via Recursive Evidence Fusion
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Online scene change detection requires an agent to detect what has changed in a previously mapped environment while it is still on site, observing from unconstrained viewpoints and without access to future observations. This causal setting is strictly harder than its offline counterpart, and online methods have consistently trailed offline accuracy. O-SCD closed that gap by treating change as a persistent property of a 3D Gaussian splatting map of the reference scene, surpassing the strongest offline methods in change detection accuracy while operating at over 10 frames per second. O-SCD optimizes a change field over the Gaussians of the reference map, refitting it to all past cue maps at every frame, a step that consumes more than half of the per-frame budget and forces accuracy to be traded against speed. We present a replay-free formulation that eliminates this trade-off. Because the reference map stays fixed, rendering the change field is a linear operation. Each new observation can therefore be carried onto the map's Gaussians directly, by a single backward pass of the renderer, which reduces multi-view fusion to an exact two-scalar recursion per Gaussian. Past observations are never stored or revisited. The self-supervised objective that O-SCD minimizes by descent also determines the decision threshold exactly, by sorting, yielding a label-free per-frame cutoff whose margin provides a selective-prediction signal. On PASLCD, our method improves mean intersection over union from 0.489 to 0.575 and throughput from 11.8 to 25.6 frames per second, even exceeding O-SCD's offline result while remaining strictly causal.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Unifying Amplitude-Phase Coupling and Reliable Endogenous Priors for Low-Light Image Enhancement
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Frequency-domain methods have shown strong potential for low-light image enhancement (LLIE) because they can effectively regulate global illumination. However, most existing methods assume that amplitude and phase can be restored independently, while overlooking their inherent spectral coupling. This artificial decoupling often leads to information inconsistency and structural distortions. To address this issue, we propose a frequency-spatial framework that jointly models spectral interaction and reliable prior guidance. We first empirically analyze the coupling between amplitude and phase and develop an Amplitude-Phase Adaptive Compensation Fusion (APACF) module. Instead of enforcing a hard separation between the two components, APACF enables their bidirectional interaction, resulting in spectrally coherent restoration. In addition, directly extracting priors from raw low-light inputs is unreliable, since severe noise and underexposure destroy critical visual content. To alleviate this problem, we introduce an Endogenous Reliability Prior (ERP). Specifically, we treat an intermediate result, preliminarily restored in the frequency domain and already close to the ground-truth illumination, as a high-fidelity source for extracting complementary pseudo-infrared and gradient cues. Based on ERP, we further design a Dual-Modal Guided Refinement Network (DGRN) to inject these purified structural cues into the decoder, thereby recovering missing fine textures more accurately. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets show that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance and consistently surpasses existing methods in both quantitative metrics and visual quality. Our code is available at https://github.com/bywlzts/Amplitude-Phase-Coupling-Net.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: RiSE: Residual Subspace Expert for Generalizable Text-Centric Image Forgery Localization
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: As AI-assisted image editing becomes increasingly prevalent, Text-Centric Image Forgery Localization (TFL) is essential for protecting trust in financial and legal records. However, we observe that existing TFL detectors predominantly rely on Full-Parameter Fine-Tuning (FPFT) and fail to generalize to unseen forgery types because FPFT can induce low-rank feature collapse and overfit training artifacts. Meanwhile, prior detectors capture diverse forgery traces with a single unified representation, making subtle traces entangled and difficult to learn. To address these challenges, we propose RiSE, a Residual Subspace Expert model that preserves pre-trained priors by freezing principal SVD components and adapting only the residual subspaces with a ViT-only segmentor to avoid feature collapse. RiSE introduces forgery-aware residual experts, where each expert is trained independently on a training subset with a particular forgery type, and we show that cross-domain localization performance improves consistently as more experts are added. At inference, we introduce Latent Perturbation Confidence (LPC), which selects the most confident expert by analytically computing the latent-perturbed output. LPC enables efficient confidence estimation with a single forward pass, avoiding repeated forward passes on perturbed samples and improving expert selection. By training on synthetic forgery data, RiSE with 1 expert outperforms prior methods on real-world forgery images by 20.4% while reducing training steps by 10 times. Scaling the number of experts to 9 yields a 35.8% gain. RiSE remains effective with DCT feature, even when the majority of the parameters is frozen with RGB-only pretraining. Code: https://github.com/KahimWong/RiSE.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Investigating Length Bias and Robustness in LVLMs for Multiple-Choice Question Answering
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) demonstrate strong performance on multiple-choice question answering (MCQA), yet their reliability under biased conditions remains underexplored. We investigate length bias, the systematic preference for longer answer options, through controlled benchmarks spanning fine-grained visual domains. LVLMs consistently favor longer options even when visually inconsistent, with accuracy dropping 2--38\% when correct answers are shorter and increasing 1--70\% when longer. This bias persists across model scales. Through layer-wise mechanistic analysis, we reveal that length bias emerges from late-layer suppression of visual evidence in favor of language-side length priors. Blurry-image experiments show that bias intensifies when visual evidence weakens, while abstention tests reveal that LVLMs struggle to refuse incorrect predictions. We propose and evaluate multiple inference-time mitigation strategies; while these provide partial improvements, none achieves deployable bias mitigation without relying on oracle information unavailable at inference time. These results underscore that inference-time interventions are insufficient, pointing to the need for architectural solutions and bias-aware training.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: SAP-Depth: Scene-Adaptive Probability Framework for Self-Supervised Monocular Depth Estimation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Self-supervised monocular depth estimation remains challenging due to the loss of fine-grained details and limited adaptability to varying scene structures. In this paper, we propose SAP-Depth, a novel architecture based on Scene-Adaptive Probabilistic. Unlike traditional methods, we introduce a Dynamic Bins mechanism powered by a Learnable Parameter Predictor, which adaptively estimates scene-specific depth distributions conditioned on the input image context. Furthermore, a Bin-wise Probability Distribution Decoder is designed to effectively fuse multi-scale representations to predict dense depth probability distributions, significantly enhancing boundary sharpness and structural recovery. Through the collaborative coupling of these proposed modules, our model achieves dynamic prediction of scene-specific depth distributions. Extensive experiments on the KITTI dataset show that SAP-Depth outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in accuracy, particularly in its ability to better preserve complex edge details. Further, tests on the Make3D dataset validate the model's excellent generalization capability and robustness.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: MOMO: Human Motion from Moving Sounds
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Human responses to sound depend not only on its semantic content, but also on the evolving spatial relationship between source and listener, conveyed through spatial audio and its temporal dynamics. Modeling human reactions to such dynamic spatial audio is important for character animation, human behavior analysis, and robotics. As of yet, existing audio-driven motion generation methods primarily focus on non-spatial or static acoustic conditions, leaving this important problem largely underexplored. To bridge this gap, we formulate the novel task of dynamic spatial-audio-driven human motion generation and introduce two motion-captured datasets. We introduce the Dynamic Spatial Audio and Motion dataset (DySAM) as the first dataset and benchmark for this task, providing synchronized binaural audio, 3D human motions, and moving sound source trajectories. Given the importance of dynamic spatial cues of sound sources, we further provide the Dynamic Spatial Audio Localization dataset (DySAL), an auxiliary binaural localization dataset that pairs diverse acoustic events with head poses and moving source trajectories to support spatial audio perception. For benchmarking, we propose MOMO for human Motion generation from Moving Sounds, a diffusion-based framework guided by three coupled principles: localization, understanding, and generation. MOMO performs localization by estimating head-centric spatial direction cues of the moving source directly from raw binaural audio, avoiding reliance on ground-truth source coordinates. It performs understanding by extracting frame-wise audio-content representations, and performs generation by conditioning motion diffusion on both semantic features and dynamic spatial cues. Experiments show that MOMO outperforms existing baselines in motion fidelity, audio-motion alignment, and physical plausibility.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: VisConf: Quality-Aware Consensus for Best-of-N in Vision-Language Model Reasoning
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Best-of-N methods improve text-only LLM reasoning by sampling multiple trajectories before selecting an answer. For Vision-Language Models (VLMs), answer frequency and model confidence alone can be insufficient, as sampled generations also vary in their engagement with the visual input. We find that distributional confidence and visual attention are complementary indicators of rollout quality. Each is limited on its own, while trajectories that show strong signals in both are more likely to be correct. Motivated by this, we introduce VisConf, a rollout-quality score that multiplicatively combines visual engagement with candidate-calibrated Self-Certainty, penalizing rollouts that are weak in either signal. We incorporate Rank-Weighted Consensus (RWC), a tuning-free aggregation rule that converts within-question VisConf ranks into answer-level vote weights. Across three VLMs on MathVista, MMMU-Pro, and MMStar, VisConf with RWC consistently outperforms strong BoN baselines. Our analysis shows particularly large gains when correct trajectories are present but underrepresented in the candidate pool.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: An Optical Music Recognition Tool for String Quartets
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: This paper presents an optical music recognition (OMR) system tailored for PDF scores of string quartet pieces. The approach begins with a SegNet-based segmentation model to localize musical regions, followed by convolutional neural networks and image processing techniques to classify and extract musical symbols. To improve rhythmic precision, dynamic programming methods enforce time signature constraints and explicitly handle tuplets. Evaluation using a longest common subsequence metric across multiple feature matrices demonstrates robust accuracy in recognizing pitch, onset, duration, and accidentals on a benchmark dataset. Code and data are available at https://github.com/lattellie/25-omr.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Contrastive Hypergraph Source-free Domain Adaptive Object Detection in Adverse Weather Conditions--Extended Version
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Adverse weather conditions such as fog, rain, snow, and low illumination introduce structured visibility degradations that severely impair object detectors trained on clear-weather data. When source data are inaccessible due to privacy or trans- mission constraints, source-free domain adaptation (SFDA) becomes necessary. However, existing SFDA methods based on pairwise contrastive learning struggle to capture high-order semantics and often suffer from agreement collapse under severe corruption. We propose REUNION, a hypergraph-guided SFDA framework for object detection in adverse weather conditions. REUNION constructs a contrastive hypergraph over target-domain object proposals, encoding high-order relations through intra-image context, weather-aware grouping, prototype-based semantic anchors, and uncertainty-aware connections between reliable and low-confidence instances. To effectively exploit these structured relations, we introduce a group-wise Hyper-InfoNCE objective that optimizes representations at the hyperedge level, enabling semantic information to propagate from confident proposals to corrupted or low-contrast instances. Experiments with diverse benchmarks demonstrate that REUNION effectively mitigates domain shifts and achieves state-of-the-art performance in SFDA settings.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Write Once, Query Many: Evolving Compact Reusable Memory for Long Videos
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Long videos often exceed the context capacity of multimodal large language models (MLLMs), while agentic search repeats costly video processing and grounding for each query. Reusable memory can amortize this cost, but must preserve information for questions unknown during construction. We propose Video-EMem, an evolvable video memory harness built on time-anchored perceptual observations. This representation combines compact free-form text with sparse images to preserve semantic content and complementary visual details across temporal scales, supporting temporal navigation without a fixed semantic schema. A Writer encodes each video once by consolidating overlapping multiscale observations, and a Reader retrieves and organizes evidence solely from the resulting memory. With the underlying models frozen, we evolve their workflows and operators using distinct feedback: query-independent source fidelity and coverage for the Writer, and QA failures in evidence localization and utilization for the Reader. Experiments support this separation for generalization beyond development queries, with our evolution strategy improving average accuracy by 7.2% over the unevolved harness. While reducing storage by about 99.86% on average relative to raw videos, Video-EMem improves Qwen3-VL-30B by an average of 2.6% across three long-video QA benchmarks over direct input of 2,048 frames. Using the same o3 answer model as the state-of-the-art agentic method, it improves average accuracy by 2.5% with lower per-query latency.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Cross-polarization pairing for label-free few-shot thin-section classification
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Few-shot classifiers of rock thin sections are meta-trained on many rock types that a petrographer has identified slide by slide, and this identification is the costly step that new collections lack. We study few-shot recognition of unseen rock types when no training slide is identified, and the only information available is what the microscope records anyway: which slide an image comes from, and whether it was taken in plane-polarized (PPL) or cross-polarized (XPL) light. We first show why generic unsupervised pseudo-tasks fit this setting poorly: the positives they find without labels are either wrong or near-duplicates of the anchor, so they teach the model little. Polarized-light microscopy provides positives that avoid both problems. The PPL and XPL views of one field show the same grains, so they are correct by construction, yet they look very different. We propose cross-polarization pairing (XPP), which treats each slide as a pseudo-class and pairs its PPL and XPL views of the same field location, so that matching must rely on grain shape and texture rather than on colour. On the Nanjing University collection of 108 rock types, with support and query images taken from different slides, XPP is the best label-free method on average over three random splits, and matches a supervised model trained on 78 identified rock types. Controls show that colour augmentation and other acquisition positives do not reproduce the gain. We also show that the image-level protocol of earlier work is saturated, and propose a cross-slide protocol in its place.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Scene-Adaptive VLA: Efficient Autonomous Driving via Dynamic Layer Routing
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models offer a promising paradigm for autonomous driving. However, the massive parameter scale of VLAs strains onboard computational resources during real-time inference. This directly increases energy consumption and limits vehicle battery range, making it critical to minimize computational overhead without compromising driving capability and explainability. Current research on efficient VLA-based driving focuses on sequential adaptation (\textit{e.g.}, Chain-of-Thought and token adjustment), leaving structural adaptation underexplored despite parameter redundancy across dynamic driving scenes. To address this gap, we propose Scene-Adaptive VLA, an efficient framework leveraging dynamic layer routing to adjust active parameters based on real-time scenes. Inspired by the temporal continuity of scenes and model predictive uncertainty, our approach characterizes model-perceived scene complexity via frame-level temporal scene variations and decision deviations. To uncover latent scene-to-parameter correspondences, we encode this characterization into scene-aware tokens, alongside two specialized queries. A budget-conditioned layer routing mechanism evaluates these refined queries to allocate a budget that determines the active parameter ratio and subsequently selects appropriate layer combinations. The entire framework is optimized end-to-end. Extensive evaluations on the Bench2Drive benchmark show that when adapted to a state-of-the-art VLA model, our approach significantly reduces inference-time computational overhead by 53.5\% with negligible degradation in driving and language capabilities. Code is available at https:github.com/yang-luvu/Scene-Adaptive-VLA.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Dynamic self-ensemble on multi-exit residual vision transformer for small-data image classification
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Vision Transformer (ViT) has garnered increased attention for image classification in recent years. However, ViT is notorious for its data-hungry problem as it achieves high-performance results when only trained on large-size datasets. In this paper, we study how ViT specifically works on small-scale datasets with limited data where the availability of image data is often constrained in practice, especially in fields such as medical imaging. To mitigate the issue, we designed a multi-stage residual ViT, dubbed ReSEViT, with the self-ensemble method to utilize multi-level information from intermediate features. Due to the complex decision boundaries for classifications, relying on a single classifier can lead to prediction errors. Hence, we propose a new learning method for ViT, named self-ensemble learning, which ensembles multi-stage classifiers in a single model. Our self-ensemble comprises a novel approach, Dynamic Learner Selection (DLS), to adaptively select the importance of different stages. ReSEViT incorporates residual token embeddings which is a ResNet-like block to model effective local structures alongside with transformer blocks in each stage. The integration of residual tokens and self-ensemble learning into a multi-stage ViT highlights the reduction in redundancy, prediction error and variance while maintaining an efficient model size for small-scale image datasets.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: SCOPE-VSR: A Broad-Coverage Training Dataset for Video Super-Resolution
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Open-domain video super-resolution (VSR) requires temporally coherent details across widely varying scenes and subjects. However, existing training datasets are often semantically imbalanced and insufficiently diverse. We address this data bottleneck with a structured curation pipeline for open-domain VSR, SCOPE. In this pipeline, we combine task-oriented video selection with hierarchical semantic rebalancing. Applying this pipeline to a large-scale collection of data sources, we construct the SCOPE-VSR dataset for training and SCOPE-test for testing. SCOPE-VSR has approximately 27k videos and provides balanced and diverse coverage of various real-world scenarios and subjects.
