However, their pretraining objectives are not designed for robot representation learning, so the resulting embeddings tend to emphasize global semantics rather than the temporally sensitive representations required for robot control. Training robot models from scratch is also undesirable due to the limited scale and high collection cost of robotics data, as well as the substantial computational burden of pre-training. In this paper, we propose SPARK (Simple Post-training for Adapting pRetrained Knowledge), a post-training method that adapts foundation models to robot control. SPARK is built on two principles: temporal abstraction, which encourages the encoder to derive compact features that preserve information essential for understanding temporal changes and action-relevant scene structure, and knowledge preservation, which aligns patch-level representations with those of the original foundation model to retain useful pretrained semantics. These objectives yield compact visual state representations that remain semantically meaningful while preserving useful prior knowledge. Experiments across multiple robotics benchmarks show that SPARK consistently improves success rates and generalization over vanilla foundation models, and further demonstrate that these gains transfer to real-world robot manipulation.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Real-Time Volumetric Light Transport Inference without a Path
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: We present a real-time method for reconstructing fully integrated pixel radiance in rendered volumetric media under direct and ambient environmental illumination, using compact, low-cost scene features and statistics. Unlike Monte Carlo denoising pipelines for volumetric rendering, which depend on computationally expensive path-traced radiance estimates, our approach directly infers the final light-transport solution from inexpensive primary-ray and environment sample evaluations. We show that these features form a near-sufficient representation of the scene, enabling accurate reconstruction at substantially lower computational cost. Using an attention-augmented image-to-image network, we demonstrate that complete pixel radiance can be inferred directly from these auxiliary features, without requiring the original radiance signal. Operating in image space also provides a more stable computational cost as the camera zooms into or out of the volume, with substantially less dependence on volume density than approaches based on explicit multiple-scattering simulation. We demonstrate real-time performance and high reconstruction accuracy in challenging volumetric cloud scenarios.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: LHNav: Long-Horizon Humanoid Navigation via Multirate Coordination and Physics-Grounded Action Data
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: We study humanoid navigation across multiple destinations under long-horizon language instructions. This task is challenging because robots must maintain progress across successive goals while continuously producing natural, stable whole-body motion through confined spaces. However, task decomposition in existing methods does not by itself ensure progress throughout execution, while waypoint-based navigation does not guarantee natural, route-faithful whole-body motion. Our key idea is to organize navigation into three complementary roles operating at different time scales: a Brain for task reasoning, a Cerebellum for local motion generation, and a Brainstem for whole-body execution. We realize this idea in LHNav, an asynchronous system that uses progress and arrival feedback to coordinate navigation goals, VLA motion-token prediction, and whole-body control. To train the Cerebellum for natural, route-faithful motion, we develop a physics-grounded data engine that improves physical tracking of motion references along collision-aware routes and pairs the resulting demonstrations with rendered visual observations. Together, these designs allow task planning to proceed alongside continuous movement and extend single-goal navigation to successive destinations with natural, route-faithful whole-body motion. In simulation, our navigation VLA outperforms OmniNav and DualVLN in single-goal success and motion smoothness, with fewer collisions and falls. Using a VLA trained only on single-goal demonstrations, LHNav achieves a 75.56% success rate on long-horizon navigation tasks. Deployment on the Unitree G1 further demonstrates single-goal navigation and zero-shot long-horizon task execution in real-world environments, including layouts with repositioned objects. Project website: https://robbyant-research.github.io/LHNav/.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Same Physics, Different Gradients: A State-of-the-Art Report on Differentiable Physics Simulation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Differentiable simulation propagates derivatives through a physics simulator, turning animation, system identification, control, and computational design into gradient-based optimization. Engines differ in the physics they model and, less visibly, in which mathematical object they differentiate. We separate two questions the literature conflates. The referent is which object the returned derivative belongs to: the finite computation that executed, the converged equation it approximates, or the continuous dynamics. The realization describes the organization of the backward pass: automatically generated differentiation, an equation-level adjoint solve, or a custom adjoint. The referent defines the target against which exactness is assessed; the implementation determines how accurately that target is approximated. Cost depends on the realization together with how the states needed by the backward pass are retained or recovered. Crossing the axes places every method and engine we classify in a cell, separates claims the literature merges, and shows that the apparent trade-off between exactness and memory follows from how methods have been built rather than from a constraint. A second, orthogonal taxonomy covers contact, where the map is non-smooth. We then ask whether a correct gradient helps. Four mechanisms by which useful gradients are lost are cataloged and measured on one testbed, where the advantage of the exact derivative over the equation-level adjoint depends on where the fitting target comes from as much as on the solver budget, and we review the evidence that zeroth-order methods can outperform simulator gradients in the regimes where those mechanisms act. The model classes, systems techniques and applications are surveyed through this lens, and we close with a reporting checklist, a released diagnostic that computes it, and a research agenda.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Harnessing Vision-Language Models for Federated Unsupervised Visual Recognition
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Federated learning (FL) is a promising research paradigm that enables collaborative model training across distributed clients without data sharing. To handle unlabeled data in local clients, existing unsupervised FL research has primarily focused on tasks like clustering and self-supervised representation learning, leaving the critical problem of unsupervised visual recognition largely unexplored. To bridge this gap, we introduce FedUR, the first framework designed for unsupervised recognition by leveraging the zero-shot capabilities of pre-trained vision-language models like CLIP. Specifically, FedUR addresses data heterogeneity through a pseudo-labeling mechanism with a class-aware data selection strategy. This strategy first estimates a global pseudo-label distribution, then allocates pseudo-labeled data to clients accordingly. To handle the uncertainty of conventional positive pseudo-labels, FedUR further incorporates class weights and a negative pseudo-labeling strategy. Furthermore, FedUR proposes a personalized prompt aggregation protocol where general visual prompts are aggregated on the server, and personalized text prompts encoding local knowledge are retained on clients. Extensive experiments demonstrate that FedUR consistently outperforms baseline methods under both label-level and feature-level distribution shifts. We believe this work paves the way for further advances in federated unsupervised recognition. Code will be available at {github.com/tim-learn/FedUR/}}.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Controlling Temporal Pseudo-Label Marginals for Stable Online Test-Time Adaptation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Continual Test-Time Adaptation (CTTA) methods update models online using a stream of unlabeled data to overcome distribution shifts encountered at test time. However, CTTA is often unstable, as it can reinforce biases in early predictions and increasingly predict only a few classes, resulting in drift or even collapse. In this paper, we identify narrowing pseudo-label class usage as an indicator of CTTA instability and quantify this behavior. Most existing methods have attempted to address this issue by either selecting reliable adaptation samples or re-weighting the loss to encourage diverse pseudo-labels, but they do not explicitly enforce a class marginal over a temporal window. Instead, we propose Sinkhorn Class-Marginal Regularization (SCALAR), a simple plug-and-play module that controls the pseudo-label distribution over a short temporal window. SCALAR works by maintaining recent predictions in a buffer, balancing their class distribution via the Sinkhorn algorithm to match a specified target distribution, and using the balanced soft targets for adaptation. Without changing the model architecture, SCALAR maintains the per-step runtime and increases the peak allocated GPU memory by only 10 MB on ImageNet-C. Our method is particularly effective on skewed, non-stationary data with severe distribution shifts, where SCALAR significantly alleviates drift and collapse when combined with existing stabilization methods based on entropy or diversity.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: VLA-MOPD: On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Task VLA Policy Consolidation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Physical intelligence requires embodied agents to ground language in observations and execute actions while retaining useful skills. Vision-language-action (VLA) policies offer a shared interface, but task-specific post-training often produces separate specialists. Consolidation is difficult: mixed-task reinforcement learning provides sparse trajectory-level credit, while offline distillation may miss student-visited observations and endpoint distillation does not supervise intermediate action-generation states. We introduce VLA Multi-teacher On-Policy Distillation (VLA-MOPD), a protocol for consolidating flow-matching VLA specialists. After acquiring task or suite experts, a shared student collects robot rollouts and queries the instruction-routed frozen teacher at each visited observation and intermediate ordinary differential equation (ODE) state. Detached per-flow-step transition targets supervise valid action chunks through a masked local matching loss; an optional reference-policy term supports retention on other tasks. Starting from one trajectory per LIBERO task, VLA-MOPD raises mean success-once from 75.4% to 98.9%, compared with 98.15% for endpoint action distillation. It improves mean RoboTwin 2.0 success from 73.0% to 89.3%; on a Piper robot, two consolidation rounds improve average success from 70.0% to 90.0%. In a near-matched Spatial-adaptation study, reference matching limits the Object suite decrease to 3.0 points, versus 13.2 without the reference term.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Mitigating SM-Level Load Imbalance in 3D Gaussian Splatting on GPUs
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables photorealistic, real-time rendering on commodity GPUs and is increasingly adopted in generative world models and autonomous driving simulators. However, existing optimizations rely on algorithmic changes that often require retraining, or on specialized accelerators that lack flexibility across evolving 3DGS variants. In this paper, we identify a fundamental inefficiency in GPU-based 3DGS rendering: severe SM-level load imbalance caused by uneven workloads across screen tiles. This imbalance creates a long execution tail, leaving most SMs idle while a few process computationally intensive tiles, particularly in large-scale urban scenes. To address this, we present a software-defined GPU scheduling approach that mitigates the execution tail. Our approach uses a persistent kernel to schedule heavy tiles first and selectively chunks outlier tiles across multiple CTAs. A lightweight per-frame policy determines when and how much to chunk using tile statistics already available in the rendering pipeline. Our approach requires neither retraining nor specialized hardware and can be applied orthogonally to existing optimizations across diverse 3DGS variants. Averaged per scene, it accelerates alpha blending by up to 2.93x on a large-scale urban scene, and by up to 5.6x on its most imbalanced frames, while retaining the original alpha blending formulation.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: How Many Exposures Does a World Model Need? Learning Unseen Game Mechanics at Test Time
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: World models enable agents to plan and learn from imagined experience, but in an unfamiliar environment they must learn its mechanics from limited interaction. A mechanic is a rule for how an action or an interaction changes part of the environment. Each occurrence of a mechanic that the model observes is one exposure. We ask how many exposures a world model needs to predict the effects of a new environment's mechanics. We address this question on ARC-AGI-3, a benchmark of interactive games defined by their programs. We introduce MechEval, which labels 69 recurring mechanics across 20 games from these programs. It scores each prediction on the cells the mechanic changes at each exposure. As a test bed, we build WARC (World model for ARC-AGI-3), a 35M-parameter vision transformer that is pretrained on other games and updates all of its parameters after each transition. On held-out games, WARC learns to predict four in five mechanics with at least 80% accuracy on the cells they change and keeps that accuracy to the end of the recordings. Half of them reach that accuracy within about 80 exposures, in a single play of the game, and without updates only one in seven does at all. In closed-loop play on the public games, WARC-Agent, which pairs WARC with a fixed graph explorer, triples the explorer's official efficiency score from 0.15 to 0.46, mostly through test-time training. On the hidden games of the Kaggle leaderboard, our entry scores 0.20.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Rethinking Radar 3D Perception: Representation Learning from Raw Spectra
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Raw radar spectra are widely viewed as too cluttered and noisy for direct representation learning, motivating handcrafted reductions, sparse point clouds, or compact Doppler descriptors in radar perception. We challenge this assumption and argue that the main limitation lies not in the raw representation itself, but in the absence of a learning objective that separates structured signal from noise. Handcrafted reductions partially address this problem but impose rigid assumptions about what constitutes signal, discarding weak yet informative structure while retaining artifacts that fit the reduction model. Once removed, such information cannot be recovered by supervised learning. We propose an alternative: structure is the component of a radar spectrum that remains reconstructable under localized corruption, while noise is the component that does not. This perspective motivates self-supervised masked modeling for dense radar spectra without predefined signal-noise separation. We instantiate it with Leakage-aware Spectral MAE, a masked autoencoder for raw radar cubes using a corruption strategy inspired by cross-bin energy spreading caused by spectral leakage. We also demonstrate the importance of Doppler organization: treating Doppler as a primary spatial dimension in an x-y-D representation, with height encoded as features, substantially outperforms naive channel stacking and enables effective learning from dense 4D spectra. Without handcrafted reductions, our approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art radar-based detectors and point-cloud-based self-supervised learning (SSL) counterparts. These results establish raw radar spectra as an effective representation for 3D perception when paired with an appropriate pretraining objective.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: AutoVLA-D: Learn a Trajectory-Geometric Condition from Reasoning for Autonomous Driving VLA
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Autoregressive VLA planning usually predicts continuous trajectories as the final output, but driving instructions often describe actions rather than ego states, which weakens direct conditioning on the final continuous trajectory. We address this gap with TrajCond, which introduces a discrete trajectory-geometric condition for VLA planning. Specifically, we represent TrajCond as a 1D-Brohan differential action trajectory and learn it with a two-stage training framework before final continuous trajectory prediction. With the simultaneous autoregressive generation of discrete and numeric trajectories, we name our method AutoVLA-D (Double). Experiments on NAVSIM navtest, nuScenes, and NeuroNCAP show that discrete trajectories are weaker as direct outputs but more effective as TrajCond, consistently improving final continuous trajectory prediction across closed-loop and open-loop driving benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/ShivaTeam/AutoVLA-D.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: V3DSAM: Semantic-Geometric Loop Verification and Geometry-Anchored Persistent Instance Mapping for Feed-Forward Dense SLAM
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: To address unreliable cross-view association in long-sequence feed-forward dense SLAM, this letter presents V3DSAM, an open-vocabulary semantic dense SLAM system that establishes physical correspondences at both the scene and object levels. The system combines feed-forward geometric estimates from VGGT-SLAM 2.0 with open-vocabulary semantic observations from SAM3. We introduce semantic-geometric dual-scale loop verification, which identifies false loop closures using pixel-level bidirectional reprojection and object-level 3D spatial correspondences, without accessing backbone-internal features. We further propose geometry-anchored persistent instance mapping, which defines physical instances through class-constrained 3D connectivity in an optimized global coordinate system and assigns global IDs without inter-frame identity propagation. The proposed verifier rejects all four false loop candidates in our TUM RGB-D evaluation, while long-sequence ScanNet experiments show improved instance identity consistency. Thus, V3DSAM reduces dependence on internal backbone features and temporal ID propagation for robust long-term cross-view association.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Direct Conditioning of Audio Diffusion Transformers on fMRI Reveals Cortical Contributions to Sound Reconstruction
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Reconstructing audio from brain activity remains challenging. Existing brain-to-audio pipelines typically map neural responses to predefined stimulus representations before synthesis. While recent work in the visual domain has explored direct conditioning on brain activity, this approach has not yet been extended to audio diffusion models. We introduce MAAS (Multi-Area Auditory Synthesis), an end-to-end framework that conditions a pretrained audio diffusion transformer on ROI-wise fMRI responses without first supervising a decoder to predict an external stimulus representation. MAAS uses region-specific projections and learned brain tokens to condition Stable Audio through a dedicated cross-attention pathway. On a 7T fMRI dataset, we demonstrate consistent improvements over baselines, including two-stage fMRI-to-latent conditioning, across both acoustic and semantic evaluation metrics. In addition, we introduce a fidelity metric grounded in a computational model of auditory neural processing, which allows us to quantify the contribution of individual auditory cortical regions to reconstructed audio representations.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Controlled Binary Assignment Flows
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: This paper introduces a geometric approach to the representation and learning of time-variant parametrizations of deep assignment flows, for binary data labelings on graphs. Each edge carries an optimally controlled parameter flow in a 2-dimensional totally geodesic submanifold, based on objectives derived from a non-local linear scale space representation of the input data. The aggregation of triplets of such flows in 5-dimensional totally geodesic submanifolds is learned from data. The fusion of these flows determines the trajectory in the high-dimensional symmetric parameter space and by geometric integration the layers of binary deep assignment flows. Numerical results demonstrate the expressivity and the limitation of our highly parallel geometric local synthesis approach to high-dimensional deep assignment flow parametrizations.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: A four-step validation protocol for radiomic survival analysis in small cohorts: a body composition case study
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary:
Gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (GEP-NET) lack prognostic biomarkers, and computed tomography (CT)-based body composition radiomics at the third lumbar vertebra (L3) is a promising candidate. Small cohorts make high-dimensional radiomic models prone to overfitting and single-split evaluations variable and optimistic.
  This methodological study proposes a four-step validation protocol for radiomic survival analysis in small cohorts: (1) false discovery rate (FDR)-corrected feature selection, (2) a dual-path comparison of prior feature selection versus embedded regularization, (3) repeated nested cross-validation (CV) and (4) a negative control with Gaussian noise features. In 78 GEP-NET patients, 535 radiomic features from five L3 compartments were used to evaluate five survival models with Harrell's concordance index (C-index), time-dependent area under the curve (AUC) and integrated Brier score (IBS).
  Step 1 selected at least one feature in 18% of outer folds under noise (nominal level 20%) versus 84% with radiomic features. The dual-path comparison showed no consistent difference between strategies. Repeated nested CV reduced variability across seeds (41% median reduction in C-index standard deviation), but not enough to distinguish models. The nested CV C-index exceeded chance by 0.07-0.15 with radiomic features but not clearly under noise (0.40-0.42 with prior feature selection, 0.47-0.55 with embedded regularization). Frequently selected features tentatively linked greater subcutaneous fat, skeletal muscle compactness and texture to better prognosis.
  These findings suggest a modest prognostic signal in L3 radiomics, with considerable uncertainty that the protocol quantifies. The protocol may transfer to other small-cohort radiomic survival studies. Code: https://github.com/marielatalaveram/radiomics-survival-validation-protocol.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Anchor Behavior, Not Parameters: Rehearsal-Free Continual Learning with a Single Shared Prompt
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Prompt-based continual learning adapts a frozen pre-trained vision transformer by tuning a small set of prompt tokens. Recently, one-prompt methods which share one single prompt across all tasks make this paradigm maximally parameter efficient. The open question is how a shared prompt can keep the knowledge of old classes while being updated for new ones. Existing methods protect old knowledge in parameter space, where they freeze task-specific prompts, expand new components, or sparsely gate which tokens receive gradients. However, this method sacrifices plasticity, yet the drift it still permits in shared tokens can corrupt the prompt's function on past classes. What must be preserved is the prompt's behavior. We propose TEA-Prompt, which couples (i) a token evaluation module that assigns each prompt token a continuous, input-conditional relevance score injected into the attention logits, softly specializing tokens across tasks without discarding any of them, and (ii) an attention-behavior anchoring loss that constrains each token's attention output around class-specific query regions using only compact Gaussian query statistics without stored old images, weighted by the token's past relevance. Anchoring the attention value allows the parameters to continue updating freely, as long as their interaction remains unchanged. TEA-Prompt achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with markedly lower forgetting on CIFAR-100, ImageNet-R, and CUB-200 with only 0.38M parameters. Code is publicy available at https://github.com/cuonga1cvp/TEA-Prompt.git

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Guiding Data Allocation for Robust Subpopulation Generalization
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Machine learning models often achieve high average accuracy in the training data while performing poorly on test data due to subpopulation shift. A common data-centric solution is to enforce balanced subgroup proportions, but full balance can be costly, infeasible, and not always necessary. In this work, we study whether balanced training data is the unique optimal configuration for robust subpopulation generalization. We extend a Gaussian feature-model framework to theoretically characterize the performance landscape across general training subgroup distributions. We show that multiple configurations, including substantially imbalanced ones, can perform comparably to the balanced one. We further derive gradient-based directions for adjusting subgroup proportions to improve adjusted accuracy and worst-group accuracy more efficiently. These findings suggest that strategically allocating data offers a more flexible and principled path to robust performance than simple balancing. The code is available at https://github.com/zhaoyingpan/subpop-data-allocation.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Deep Algebraic Fitting for Multiple Circle Primitives Extraction from Raw Point Clouds
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: The shape of circle is one of fundamental geometric primitives of man-made engineering objects. Thus, extraction of circles from scanned point clouds is a quite important task in 3D geometry data processing. However, existing circle extraction methods either are sensitive to the quality of raw point clouds when classifying circle-boundary points, or require well-designed fitting functions when regressing circle parameters. To relieve the challenges, we propose an end-to-end Point Cloud Circle Algebraic Fitting Network (Circle-Net) based on a synergy of deep circle-boundary point feature learning and weighted algebraic fitting. First, we design a circle-boundary learning module, which considers local and global neighboring contexts of each point, to detect all potential circle-boundary points. Second, we develop a deep feature based circle parameter learning module for weighted algebraic fitting, without designing any weight metric, to avoid the influence of outliers during fitting. Unlike most of the cutting-edge circle extraction wisdoms, the proposed classification-and-fitting modules are originally co-trained with a comprehensive loss to enhance the quality of extracted circles.Comparisons on the established dataset and real-scanned point clouds exhibit clear improvements of Circle-Net over SOTAs in terms of both noise-robustness and extraction accuracy. We will release our code, model, and data for both training and evaluation on GitHub upon publication.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: AI-Generated Images as Data Source: The Dawn of Synthetic Era
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: The advancement of visual intelligence is intrinsically tethered to the availability of large-scale data. In parallel, generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) has unlocked the potential to create synthetic images that closely resemble real-world photographs. This prompts a compelling inquiry: how much visual intelligence could benefit from the advance of generative AI? This paper explores the innovative concept of harnessing these AI-generated images as new data sources, reshaping traditional modeling paradigms in visual intelligence. In contrast to real data, AI-generated data exhibit remarkable advantages, including unmatched abundance and scalability, the rapid generation of vast datasets, and the effortless simulation of edge cases. Built on the success of generative AI models, we examine the potential of their generated data in a range of applications, from training machine learning models to simulating scenarios for computational modeling, testing, and validation. We probe the technological foundations that support this groundbreaking use of generative AI, engaging in an in-depth discussion on the ethical, legal, and practical considerations that accompany this transformative paradigm shift. Through an exhaustive survey of current technologies and applications, this paper presents a comprehensive view of the synthetic era in visual intelligence. A project associated with this paper can be found at https://github.com/mwxely/AIGS .

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Towards Multi-domain Face Landmark Detection with Synthetic Data from Diffusion model
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Recently, deep learning-based facial landmark detection for in-the-wild faces has achieved significant improvement. However, there are still challenges in face landmark detection in other domains (e.g. cartoon, caricature, etc). This is due to the scarcity of extensively annotated training data. To tackle this concern, we design a two-stage training approach that effectively leverages limited datasets and the pre-trained diffusion model to obtain aligned pairs of landmarks and face in multiple domains. In the first stage, we train a landmark-conditioned face generation model on a large dataset of real faces. In the second stage, we fine-tune the above model on a small dataset of image-landmark pairs with text prompts for controlling the domain. Our new designs enable our method to generate high-quality synthetic paired datasets from multiple domains while preserving the alignment between landmarks and facial features. Finally, we fine-tuned a pre-trained face landmark detection model on the synthetic dataset to achieve multi-domain face landmark detection. Our qualitative and quantitative results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing methods on multi-domain face landmark detection.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: ProCreate, Don't Reproduce! Propulsive Energy Diffusion for Creative Generation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: In this paper, we propose ProCreate, a simple and easy-to-implement method to improve sample diversity and creativity of diffusion-based image generative models and to prevent training data reproduction. ProCreate operates on a set of reference images and actively propels the generated image embedding away from the reference embeddings during the generation process. We propose FSCG-8 (Few-Shot Creative Generation 8), a few-shot creative generation dataset on eight different categories -- encompassing different concepts, styles, and settings -- in which ProCreate achieves the highest sample diversity and fidelity. Furthermore, we show that ProCreate is effective at preventing replicating training data in a large-scale evaluation using training text prompts. Code and FSCG-8 are available at https://github.com/Agentic-Learning-AI-Lab/procreate-diffusion-public. The project page is available at https://procreate-diffusion.github.io.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: ViDE: Tuning-Free Video Coherence via Temporal Attention Reweighting and Prompt Blending
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Despite the substantial progress in long video generation, multi-prompt synthesis often encounters inconsistencies resulting from the training-inference gap caused by length extension techniques and coarse prompt interpolation. To overcome these issues, we propose the Video Diffusion with hidden states Editing (ViDE) framework, which consists of two key components. The first is the Time-frequency based Temporal Attention Reweighting (TiTAR) algorithm, which leverages the relationship between inconsistencies and diagonal elements of temporal attention. By reweighting the attention scores via the Discrete Short-Time Fourier Transform (DSTFT), TiTAR effectively reduces frame inconsistencies, a capability further corroborated by a Fourier-based analysis. The second component, PromptBlend, reduces inconsistencies in multi-prompt settings through fine-grained prompt alignment and adaptive interpolation, enabling smooth semantic transitions. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of ViDE, demonstrating consistent and significant improvements over multiple baselines.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Paleoinspired Vision: From Exploring Colour Vision Evolution to Inspiring Camera Design
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: The evolution of colour vision is captivating, as it reveals the adaptive strategies of extinct species while simultaneously inspiring innovations in modern imaging technology. In this study, we present a simplified model of visual transduction in the retina, introducing a novel opsin layer. We quantify evolutionary pressures by measuring machine vision recognition accuracy on colour images shaped by specific opsins. Building on this, we develop an evolutionary conservation optimisation algorithm to reconstruct the spectral sensitivity of opsins, enabling mutation-driven adaptations to more effectively spot fruits or predators. This model condenses millions of years of evolution into seconds using GPU, providing an experimental framework to test long-standing hypotheses in evolutionary biology, such as vision of early mammals, primate trichromacy from gene duplication, retention of colour blindness, blue-shift of fish rod and multiple rod opsins with bioluminescence. Beyond validating existing paleontological hypotheses, our model further enables speculative explorations of hypothetical species, such as organisms with visual systems adapted to Martian conditions. These constitute our contributions to AI for life science and neuroscience. Besides, the principles derived from these biological studies can translate into practical engineering solutions. In practice, our findings suggest a minimalist yet effective approach to task-specific camera filter design, optimising the spectral response function to meet application-driven demands. Code repository: https://github.com/luyijie-research/PaleVision.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: LFX: Fusion-Form-Flexible Light Field Modeling for Dense Semantic Segmentation and Salient Object Detection
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Two distinct light field (LF) observation forms, namely sub-aperture images (S.Aperture images) and focal stack (FS), correspond to two fusion settings: the central image with S.Aperture images (CS) and the central image with FS (CF). Existing LF perception methods are typically form-specific, while a modeling design that can be separately instantiated under either setting remains underexplored. To address this gap, we present LFX, a form-flexible LF perception framework. Here, ``X'' represents the LF observation form, indicating that the one modeling design can be separately instantiated under two fusion settings (CS and CF). Specifically, we propose Field-of-Parallax Angular Subspace Modeling (FoP-ASM), which maps the feature difference between each auxiliary observation and the central image to an observation-specific angular marker. This avoids pairwise modeling among auxiliary observations and form-specific geometric assumptions. Meanwhile, a shared manifold subspace and the associated regularization losses constrain the angular residuals within a common feature space, promoting semantic consistency across auxiliary observations. Extensive evaluations across three LF datasets show that LFX achieves state-of-the-art results across distinct LF forms. Under the S.Aperture images and FS settings, respectively, LFX reduces MAE by 12.12%/20.59% on DUTLF-V2 and by 6.15%/7.69% on HFUT, while achieving the best performance on UrbanLF-real. The source code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/FeiT-FeiTeng/LFX.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: RefRef: A Dataset and Benchmark for Reconstructing Refractive and Reflective Objects
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Modern 3D reconstruction and novel view synthesis approaches have demonstrated strong performance on scenes with opaque, non-refractive objects. However, most assume straight light paths and therefore cannot properly handle refractive and reflective materials. The lack of datasets specialized for these effects has impeded efforts to fairly and thoroughly evaluate performance and thereby make progress in this domain. Most existing datasets focus on opaque scenes, while those targeting refractive objects are often limited to thin glass with negligible ray bending, untinted single-material objects, or backgrounds treated as infinitely-distant, leaving key failure modes under strong refraction untested. To address this gap, we introduce the RefRef dataset. It contains 150 synthetic and 60 real scenes spanning varying levels of geometric complexity and diverse background types that expose the limitations of existing methods. For the purpose of benchmarking, we also provide an oracle method that, given the object geometry and refractive indices, calculates accurate light paths for neural rendering, and a simple two-stage baseline that relaxes these assumptions. We evaluate these against state-of-the-art methods and show that the task is far from solved.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Speculative Decoding Reimagined for Multimodal Large Language Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) deliver strong performance across vision-language tasks but suffer from high autoregressive decoding latency. Although speculative decoding can accelerate Large Language Models (LLMs) without changing their output distribution, directly applying existing approaches to MLLMs yields limited speedups because text and visual tokens exhibit distinct characteristics. We present Multimodal Speculative Decoding (MSD), a framework specifically designed for efficient MLLM inference. MSD is motivated by two key observations: text and visual tokens should be handled separately during drafting, and an effective draft model requires both strong language modeling and visual perception capabilities. Accordingly, MSD decouples text and visual token processing in the draft model and applies token-specific strategies to improve drafting efficiency. We further introduce a two-stage training strategy. The draft model is first trained on text-only instruction-tuning data to strengthen its language modeling ability and is then progressively exposed to multimodal data to develop visual perception while preserving its language competence. Extensive experiments across multimodal benchmarks demonstrate that MSD achieves up to $2.29\times$ inference speedup for LLaVA-1.5-7B and $2.46\times$ for LLaVA-1.5-13B without sacrificing generation quality. These results establish MSD as an effective and general approach for accelerating multimodal autoregressive generation. Our code is available at https://github.com/Lyn-Lucy/MSD

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Neurosymbolic Object-Centric Learning with Distant Supervision
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Neurosymbolic learning can use symbolic rules to provide supervision for latent concepts from weak labels, but it commonly assumes that the entities referenced by these rules are already specified. Object-centric models decompose images into slot-like representations; however, such slots are not necessarily aligned with the predicates required for symbolic reasoning. We investigate object-centric neurosymbolic learning under distant supervision, where the object-level arguments of a logic program are learned directly from images using only global task labels. We introduce DeepPbjectLog, a probabilistic neurosymbolic model that integrates a slot-based perceptual encoder with a probabilistic logic layer. The encoder predicts objectness and class probabilities for candidate object representations, while the logic layer marginalizes over latent objectness and class assignments to compute the likelihood of the observed label. This formulation provides a differentiable task-level learning signal for object-centric perception without requiring per-object labels, masks, bounding boxes, or heuristic set matching. Evaluations across diverse visual reasoning tasks demonstrate that DeepObjectLog achieves superior out-of-distribution generalization to compositional, object-count, and rule shifts compared to neural object-centric and standard neurosymbolic baselines.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Transferring Visual Explainability from Self-Explaining to Prediction-Only Vision Transformers via Task Arithmetic
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: In image classification scenarios where both prediction and explanation efficiency are required, self-explaining models that perform both tasks in a single inference are effective. However, for users who already have prediction-only models, training a new self-explaining model from scratch is costly in both labeling and computation. This study proposes a method to transfer the visual explanation capability of self-explaining Vision Transformer (ViT) models learned in a source domain to prediction-only, zero-shot-capable ViT models based on vision-language models (VLMs) in a target domain via task arithmetic, without target-side explanation supervision. The proposed method endows target models with explanation capability by adding an explainability vector induced by explanation supervision in the source domain based on the task arithmetic framework. Experiments on 10 diverse target datasets show that a single explainability vector learned on ImageNet-1k augmented with patch-level explanation supervision transfers consistently, improving explanation quality while largely preserving classification accuracy. Within-model faithfulness evaluation and comparisons with control vectors (e.g., random vectors of the same norm) show that the transferred explanations are faithful to the model's own predictions and that the effect is specific to the explainability vector. Beyond the transfer itself, we further investigate whether transfer success can be anticipated a priori from model-internal features alone, and find that, for a fixed source, a small set of such features carries non-trivial signal about the transfer outcome on held-out targets. Code is available at https://github.com/yuyay/explainability_vector.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: IKOD: Image-Attention-Guided Key-Value Merging against Object Hallucination in the Decoding of Large Vision-Language Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) exhibit strong visual understanding and language generation capabilities yet remain prone to object hallucination, producing plausible descriptions unsupported by the input image. Analyzing generation dynamics across eight diverse LVLMs, we observe that cross-modal visual attention steadily decays as generation unfolds because appended text tokens continuously expand the softmax denominator; consequently, hallucinated objects consistently appear later and under lower image attention than grounded mentions. Unlike existing training-free remedies that rely on input perturbations or external models, we propose IKOD (Image-attention-guided Key-value merging against Object hallucination in Decoding), a collaborative decoder that directly compresses the competing text context within the native key-value (KV) cache. At each step, IKOD keeps visual tokens intact and merges low-attention text entries into a compact auxiliary cache, fusing the resulting image-focused distribution with the base branch to correct ungrounded predictions while preserving linguistic fluency. An adaptive variant (IKOD-A) further schedules collaboration strength online from the measured attention decay under a single universal configuration. Extensive experiments across hallucination and general multimodal benchmarks on eight diverse LVLMs demonstrate that IKOD and IKOD-A consistently mitigate object hallucination while preserving object recall and general multimodal capabilities at minimal inference cost. Code is available at https://github.com/jiabingyang01/IKOD.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Language-Aware Information Maximization for Transductive Few-Shot CLIP
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Transductive few-shot learning has triggered an abundant literature focusing on vision-only models, but is still at a nascent stage within the recent context of foundational vision-language models (VLMs). Only a few recent methods addressed the problem, pointing to the potential of tranduction in VLMs and to the need for VLM-tailored methods. Building on this momentum, we leverage information-theoretic concepts and recent progress in parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT), developing a highly competitive transductive few-shot CLIP method. Specifically, we introduce a novel Language-aware Information MaximizatiOn (LIMO) loss integrating three complementary terms: (i) the mutual information between the vision inputs and the textual class descriptions; (ii) a Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence penalizing deviation of the network's probabilistic outputs from the text-driven zero-shot predictions; and (iii) a standard cross-entropy loss based on the labeled shots. Furthermore, we challenge the commonly followed fine-tuning practices in the context of transductive few-shot learning, and explore PEFT strategies, completely overlooked in this context. Surprisingly, we observe substantial boosts in performances, which points to the potential of adapting a subset of the model's parameters in the transductive few-shot setting. We report comprehensive evaluations, which show that LIMO outperforms the very recent transductive few-shot CLIP methods by a large margin and yields significant gains over the best-performing inductive methods. Our code is publicly available at:https://github.com/ghassenbaklouti/LIMO

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Exploring the Capabilities of Large Language Model Encoders for Image-Text Retrieval in Chest X-rays
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Multimodal learning from paired medical images and clinical text is a central challenge in medical data-driven informatics, where effective cross-modal alignment is critical for scalable analysis and retrieval. In chest radiography, vision-language pretraining is constrained by heterogeneous radiology reports that contain abbreviations, impression-only notes, and institution-specific writing styles. Unlike general-domain settings, naively aggregating large collections of noisy reports can plateau or even degrade multimodal learning when reporting styles differ substantially. We propose a domain-adapted bidirectional large language model text encoder for chest radiograph reports, trained with masked token prediction and supervised contrastive learning on stylistically diverse but clinically equivalent report variants to produce robust, generalizable text embeddings. We then integrate this encoder into a dual-tower contrastive vision-language framework using parameter-efficient adaptation to improve image-text alignment. Across 1.6 million paired studies from public datasets and a de-identified hospital cohort, the proposed models improve bidirectional retrieval accuracy and external generalization, achieving GREEN scores of 0.308 on MIMIC-CXR and 0.618 on Open-I, while reducing the degradation observed when abbreviation-rich, impression-only hospital reports are added to training.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: ChartHal: A Fine-grained Framework Evaluating Hallucination of Large Vision Language Models in Chart Understanding
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have recently demonstrated remarkable progress, yet hallucination remains a critical barrier, particularly in chart understanding, which requires sophisticated perceptual and cognitive abilities as well as rigorous factual accuracy. While prior work has investigated hallucinations and chart comprehension independently, their intersection remains largely unexplored. To address this gap, we present ChartHal, a benchmark that features a fine-grained taxonomy of hallucination scenarios in chart understanding, along with a human-validated dataset of 1,062 samples. Our evaluation shows that state-of-the-art LVLMs suffer from severe hallucinations on ChartHal, including proprietary models such as GPT-5 and o4-mini, which achieve only 34.46% and 22.79% accuracy, respectively. Further analysis reveals that questions involving information absent from or contradictory to charts are especially likely to trigger hallucinations, underscoring the urgent need for more robust mitigation strategies. Code and data are available at https://github.com/ymcui/ChartHal

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Entropy Guided Dynamic Patch Segmentation for Time Series Transformers
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Patch-based transformers have emerged as efficient and improved long-horizon modeling architectures for time series modeling. Yet, existing approaches rely on temporally-agnostic patch construction, where arbitrary starting positions and fixed lengths fracture temporal coherence by splitting natural transitions across boundaries. This naive segmentation often disrupts short-term dependencies and weakens representation learning. We propose a novel Entropy-Guided Dynamic Patch Encoder (EntroPE), as a temporally informed framework that dynamically detects transition points via conditional entropy and dynamically places patch boundaries. This preserves temporal structure while retaining the computational benefits of patching. EntroPE consists of two key modules, namely an Entropy-based Dynamic Patcher (EDP) that applies information-theoretic criteria to locate natural temporal shifts and determine patch boundaries, and an Adaptive Patch Encoder (APE) that employs pooling and cross-attention to capture intra-patch dependencies and produce fixed-size latent representations. Extensive experiments on long-term forecasting, classification, and anomaly detection demonstrate that the proposed method improves both accuracy and efficiency, establishing entropy-guided dynamic patching as a promising new paradigm for time series modeling. Code is available at https://github.com/Sachithx/EntroPE.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Towards Continual Expansion of Data Coverage: Automatic Text-guided Edge-case Synthesis
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: The performance of deep neural networks is strongly influenced by the quality of their training data. However, mitigating dataset bias by manually curating challenging edge cases remains a major bottleneck. To address this, we propose an automated pipeline for text-guided edge-case synthesis. Our approach employs a Large Language Model, fine-tuned via preference learning, to rephrase image captions into diverse textual prompts that steer a Text-to-Image model toward generating difficult visual scenarios. Evaluated on the FishEye8K object detection benchmark, our method achieves superior robustness, surpassing both naive augmentation and manually engineered prompts. This work establishes a scalable framework that shifts data curation from manual effort to automated, targeted synthesis, offering a promising direction for developing more reliable and continuously improving AI systems. Code is available at https://github.com/gokyeongryeol/ATES.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Blind Image Restoration via Merging the Manifold Hypothesis, Kernel Method and a Diffusion-like Flow
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Blind Image Restoration (BIR) aims to restore degraded images without knowledge of either the type or severity of the degradation. This is a challenging ill-posed inverse problem for which an image prior is essential. We view the prior of an image class as a probability distribution supported on a low-dimensional manifold embedded in the high-dimensional image space. Existing generative approaches primarily model the probability distribution, while the geometric structure is implicit or disregarded. Conversely, geometric approaches do not account for the non-uniform probability distribution on the manifold. We propose a geometric-probabilistic framework for BIR that models these aspects. The probability distribution on the manifold is approximated using a kernel-based method, while a distance from the manifold function induces a geometry-based probability function on the ambient space. This formulation leads to the (Latent) Manifold-Probabilistic Projection Model ((L)MPPM), a restoration model defined in both image and latent spaces. (L)MPPM induces a flow guided by a score field that jointly incorporates geometric and probabilistic information. Evaluated on image restoration tasks and datasets, (L)MPPM consistently outperforms existing approaches, providing empirical evidence for the benefit of incorporating both geometric and probabilistic information into the image prior.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Test-Time Defense Against Adversarial Attacks via Stochastic Resonance of Latent Ensembles
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: We propose a test-time defense mechanism against adversarial attacks: imperceptible image perturbations that significantly alter the predictions of a model. Unlike existing methods that rely on feature filtering or smoothing, which can lead to information loss, we propose to "combat noise with noise" by leveraging stochastic resonance to enhance robustness while minimizing information loss. Our approach introduces small translational perturbations to the input image, aligns the transformed feature embeddings, and aggregates them before mapping back to the original reference image. This can be expressed in a closed-form formula, which can be deployed on diverse existing network architectures without introducing additional network modules or fine-tuning for specific attack types. The resulting method is entirely training-free, architecture-agnostic, and attack-agnostic. Empirical results show state-of-the-art robustness on image classification and, for the first time, establish a generic test-time defense for dense prediction tasks, including stereo matching and optical flow, highlighting the method's versatility and practicality. Specifically, relative to clean (unperturbed) performance, our method recovers up to 68.1% of the accuracy loss on image classification, 71.9% on stereo matching, and 29.2% on optical flow under various types of adversarial attacks.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: D2D: Detector-to-Differentiable Critic for Improved Numeracy in Text-to-Image Generation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models have achieved strong performance in semantic alignment, yet they still struggle with generating the correct number of objects specified in prompts. Existing approaches typically incorporate auxiliary counting networks as external critics to enhance numeracy. However, since these critics must provide gradient guidance during generation, they are restricted to regression-based models that are inherently differentiable, thus excluding detector-based models with superior counting ability, whose count-via-enumeration nature is non-differentiable. To overcome this, we propose Detector-to-Differentiable (D2D), a novel framework that transforms non-differentiable detection models into differentiable critics, leveraging their superior counting ability to guide numeracy generation. Specifically, we design custom activation functions to convert detector logits into soft binary indicators, which are then used to optimize the noise prior at inference time with pre-trained T2I models. Our extensive experiments on SDXL-Turbo, SD-Turbo, and Pixart-DMD across four benchmarks of varying complexity (low-density, high-density, and multi-object scenarios) demonstrate consistent and substantial improvements in object counting accuracy (e.g., boosting up to 13.7% on D2D-Small, a 400-prompt, low-density benchmark), with minimal degradation in overall image quality and computational overhead. Project page: https://nobliney.github.io/d2d/.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: ALICE-LRI: A General Method for Lossless Range Image Generation for Spinning LiDAR Sensors without Calibration Metadata
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: 3D LiDAR sensors are widely used in autonomous navigation, environmental monitoring, and precision mapping. Their point clouds are often projected into 2D range images for efficient processing, but conventional projection methods can lose points because of geometric inconsistencies. We present ALICE-LRI (Automatic LiDAR Intrinsic Calibration Estimation for Lossless Range Images), a metadata-free method for lossless range-image generation from calibrated spinning multi-beam LiDAR point clouds. It requires neither factory calibration files, packet-level data, nor beam identifiers, and targets operating regimes where scanlines contain enough returns for reliable parameter estimation. The method estimates the intrinsic calibration parameters relevant to projection, including beam configuration, angular distributions, and per-beam geometric corrections. Evaluation on the complete KITTI and DurLAR datasets yielded zero lost points across all point clouds. Reconstruction deviations remain below manufacturer-reported range-performance specifications, while the method runs in real time. A compression case study also shows improved reconstruction quality and a better quality-compression trade-off for a downstream application. These results enable range-image-based LiDAR processing in applications that require high measurement fidelity and preservation of acquired geometric information.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Measurement 294 (2027) 123662

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Edge Assisted Multi-Camera Vehicle Tracking Framework for Real-Time and Scalable Deployment
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Cameras are a core sensing modality in modern intelligent transportation systems (ITS), providing rich visual information on road-user activities. Multi-Camera Vehicle Tracking (MCVT) uses this data to reconstruct vehicle trajectories across camera networks, supporting applications such as traffic flow prediction and optimisation. However, most existing MCVT studies emphasise tracking accuracy while paying limited attention to real-time performance and scalability, both essential for real-world and city-scale deployment. To address this gap, we propose Edge-Assisted, Scalable and Efficient MCVT (EASE-MCVT), a distributed edge--server framework designed for real-time throughput and scalable operation. On the edge side, each camera stream is processed through object detection, single-camera tracking, geo-mapping and feature extraction, while only lightweight metadata, including vehicle locations and appearance features, is sent to the central server for cross-camera association. To improve both tracking accuracy and system efficiency, EASE-MCVT is optimised from algorithmic and system perspectives. Algorithmically, it introduces a dynamic workload scheme for tracklet-level feature extraction, a server-side re-match module to reconnect fragmented tracklets, and a self-supervised camera link model that learns spatio-temporal constraints to accelerate and stabilise cross-camera association. Systemically, it integrates production-oriented data engineering components to standardise deployment and data exchange for large-scale operation. To the best of our knowledge, EASE-MCVT is the first MCVT framework explicitly designed to address both real-time performance and scalability in a distributed edge--server setting. Experiments on the RoundaboutHD and CityFlow datasets demonstrate real-time throughput with competitive tracking accuracy, paving the way for city-wide real-time traffic management.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Matching-Based Few-Shot Semantic Segmentation Models Are Interpretable by Design
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Few-Shot Semantic Segmentation (FSS) models achieve strong performance in segmenting novel classes with minimal labeled examples, yet their decision-making processes remain largely opaque. Explainable AI has matured on standard computer vision tasks, but not on FSS, where an explanation would tell a practitioner which support pixels the prediction rested on and which examples to provide next. We argue that matching-based FSS models are interpretable by design: their query-support similarity scores, once normalized and processed, attribute the prediction to individual support pixels. Our approach, Affinity Explainer (AffEx), makes this intrinsic interpretability explicit by extracting attribution maps directly from matching scores at multiple feature levels, without requiring gradients or external perturbations. We extend the standard causal metrics for evaluating explanations to the FSS domain and propose additional metrics to better capture the practical utility of explanations in few-shot scenarios. Experiments on two FSS benchmarks, covering seven architectures that range from classical matching-based models to recent pipelines built on vision foundation models (DINOv2/v3, SAM, SAM2) and a prototype-based head, show that AffEx outperforms adapted standard attribution methods at nearly every evaluation point, and that the gain comes from the matching mechanism itself. On pipelines whose segmentation stage transforms the matching output, the same evaluation doubles as a diagnostic of where the decision is made, and on the prototype-based head AffEx subsumes the prototype-style read-out as a special case. Qualitatively, the attribution maps expose how each architecture resolves the support set, and we show how they guide model diagnosis. Code is available at https://github.com/pasqualedem/AffinityExplainer.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Dual-Granularity Semantic Prompting for Language Guidance Infrared Small Target Detection
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Infrared small target detection remains challenging due to limited feature representation and severe background interference, resulting in sub-optimal performance. While recent CLIP-inspired methods attempt to leverage textual guidance for detection, they are hindered by inaccurate text descriptions and reliance on manual annotations. To overcome these limitations, we propose DGSPNet, an end-to-end language prompt-driven framework. Our approach integrates dual-granularity semantic prompts: coarse-grained textual priors (e.g., 'infrared image', 'small target') and fine-grained personalized semantic descriptions derived through visual-to-textual mapping within the image space. This design not only facilitates learning fine-grained semantic information but also can inherently leverage language prompts during inference without relying on any annotation requirements. By fully leveraging the precision and conciseness of text descriptions, we further introduce a text-guide channel attention (TGCA) mechanism and text-guide spatial attention (TGSA) mechanism that enhances the model's sensitivity to potential targets across both low- and high-level feature spaces. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method significantly improves detection accuracy and achieves state-of-the-art performance on three benchmark datasets.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: FIELDS: Face reconstruction with accurate Inference of Expression using Learning with Direct Supervision
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Monocular 3D face reconstruction estimates the parameters of a 3D morphable face model (3DMM) from a single image, providing an explicit geometric representation for facial expression analysis. Owing to the scarcity of paired 2D images and 3D facial meshes, most methods are trained in a self-supervised manner by rendering the predicted face and minimizing image-level reconstruction losses, such as photometric and landmark errors, against the input image. However, these losses enforce visual alignment but do not ensure that the predicted parameters preserve affective information. Recent methods add image-level emotion consistency loss, but it can be satisfied by exaggerating facial deformations. To address these issues, we propose FIELDS (Face reconstruction with accurate Inference of Expression using Learning with Direct Supervision), which learns affect-informative expression representations in the FLAME parameter space. Specifically, FIELDS augments 2D self-supervised reconstruction with scan-derived expression anchoring and a parameter-space emotion loss. During training, scan-fitted targets directly constrain expression-related FLAME parameters to discourage exaggerated deformations, while a jointly trained emotion head uses discrete emotion and continuous valence--arousal annotations to make the predicted parameters informative for affect analysis. Experiments show that FIELDS improves affective utility from the predicted parameters in both within- and cross-dataset settings. Notably, it also achieves lower reconstruction errors overall and across most facial regions than the comparison baselines under both rigid and similarity alignment.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: UniDoc: Towards Unified Thinking in Documents
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Answering questions over long, visually rich documents demands both cross-page structural reasoning and fine-grained visual understanding. Existing approaches sacrifice one for the other: retrieval-augmented methods fragment documents and lose inter-page structure; monolithic vision-language models preserve structure but scale poorly beyond a few pages. This impasse stems from a false premise: that the macroscopic task of evidence retrieval and the microscopic task of detailed reasoning must either be split into separate systems or be processed identically. By decoupling their perceptual resolutions rather than their architectures, a single model can achieve the structural holism of monolithic processing alongside the efficiency of targeted retrieval. UniDoc realizes this through two resolution-adaptive stages: a Fast Reading stage processes all pages at low resolution to structurally identify evidence pages, and a Focused Thinking stage re-processes only those pages at high resolution for multimodal inference. To train this pipeline, we construct 30K multi-hop reasoning instances with stage-level supervision. On MMLongBench-Doc, UniDoc yields relative accuracy gains of 55.7% on Qwen2.5-VL-7B and 16.9% on Qwen3-VL-8B, while significantly reducing token cost relative to uniform high-resolution processing. Error analysis identifies page retrieval and fine-grained visual reasoning as the remaining bottlenecks, delineating concrete targets for future work.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Spectral Complex Autoencoder Pruning: A Fidelity-Guided Criterion for Extreme Structured Channel Compression
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: We propose Spectral Complex Autoencoder Pruning (SCAP), a reconstruction-based criterion that measures functional redundancy at the level of individual output channels. For each convolutional layer, we construct a complex interaction field by pairing the full multi-channel input activation as the real part with a single output-channel activation (spatially aligned and broadcast across input channels) as the imaginary part. We transform this complex field to the frequency domain and train a low-capacity autoencoder to reconstruct normalized spectra. Channels whose spectra are reconstructed with high fidelity are interpreted as lying close to a low-dimensional manifold captured by the autoencoder and are therefore more compressible; conversely, channels with low fidelity are retained as they encode information that cannot be compactly represented by the learned manifold. This yields an importance score (optionally fused with the filter L1 norm) that supports simple threshold-based pruning and produces a structurally consistent pruned network. On VGG16 trained on CIFAR-10, at a fixed threshold of 0.6, we obtain 90.11% FLOP reduction and 96.30% parameter reduction with an absolute Top-1 accuracy drop of 1.67% from a 93.44% baseline after fine-tuning, demonstrating that spectral reconstruction fidelity of complex interaction fields is an effective proxy for channel-level redundancy under aggressive compression.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: The pretraining domain outweighs the training objective in setting the privacy-utility trade-off of differentially private medical image analysis
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Differential privacy limits how much each training image can influence a medical imaging model but lowers its diagnostic accuracy. Pretrained weights reduce this loss. It is unknown whether the pretraining objective or domain improves accuracy more. Here we train chest radiograph classifiers under differential privacy from five starting points on 591,884 radiographs from five datasets. We show that supervised pretraining on chest radiographs ranks first in 24 of 25 combinations of dataset and privacy setting. Measured by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, its lead over supervised pretraining on natural images is 2.6% without privacy and 15.3% at the strictest budget. From that starting point, changing the domain improves this area 2.2 to 3.7 times more than changing the objective. Private pretraining on chest radiographs lowers this area by about 5% under privacy but outperforms the three starting points without patient data at the strictest budget. Under privacy, supervised chest radiograph pretraining leads in the worst-performing demographic subgroup.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: SANEval: Open-Vocabulary Compositional Benchmarks with Failure-mode Diagnosis
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Text-to-image (T2I) models struggle with compositional prompts requiring multiple objects, bound attributes, accurate counts, or spatial relations. Existing benchmarks face limits from fixed detector vocabularies, aggregated scores, and varying human-validation protocols. We introduce SANEval (Spatial, Attribute, and Numeracy Evaluation), an open-vocabulary compositional benchmark with two key contributions: (i) a public dataset of ~5,250 prompts paired with images from six state-of-the-art T2I models, split into algorithmically generated Simple and fully human-written Hard partitions across five compositional tasks, and (ii) a modular evaluation pipeline combining an LLM prompt parser, an open-vocabulary detector with LLM synonym expansion, and scorers for attribute binding, spatial relations, and numeracy. Each scorer emits numerical scores and diagnostic feedback for missing, extra, or mis-bound elements. Validated against human ratings (n = 500), SANEval achieves positive Pearson correlations across all categories (overall r = 0.222), outperforming CompBench++ (-0.016) and GenEval (-0.030). A manual audit of 24,012 detections shows 96.58% precision, with ablation confirming that synonym expansion is critical to pipeline performance. Dataset: [https://huggingface.co/datasets/saneval/saneval-release](https://huggingface.co/datasets/saneval/saneval-release). Pipeline: [https://github.com/nielseni6/saneval](https://github.com/nielseni6/saneval).

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Vision Transformers for Zero-Shot Clustering of Animal Images: A Comparative Benchmarking Study
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Manual labelling of animal images remains a significant bottleneck in ecological research, limiting the scale and efficiency of biodiversity monitoring efforts. This study investigates whether state-of-the-art Vision Transformer (ViT) foundation models can reduce thousands of unlabelled animal images directly to species-level clusters. We present a comprehensive benchmarking framework evaluating five ViT models combined with five dimensionality reduction techniques and four clustering algorithms, two supervised and two unsupervised, across 60 species (30 mammals and 30 birds), with each test using a random subset of 200 validated images per species. We investigate when clustering succeeds at species-level, where it fails, and whether clustering within the species-level reveals ecologically meaningful patterns such as sex, age, or phenotypic variation. Our primary, fully unsupervised finding is that DINOv3 embeddings with t-SNE and HDBSCAN reach a species-level V-measure of 0.943 with no prior knowledge of the number of species, rejecting only 1.14% of images as outliers requiring expert review. Assigning one label per cluster reduces manual labelling actions by 98.3%, with 94.6% of clustered images labelled correctly, close to the accuracy of manual annotation. When the true number of species is supplied, supervised hierarchical clustering raises this to 0.958, which we report as an upper bound as the species count is typically unknown in real deployments. We further demonstrate robustness to realistic long-tailed distributions of species and show that intentional over-clustering can reveal intra-specific variation including age classes, sexual dimorphism, and pelage differences. We introduce an open-source benchmarking toolkit and provide recommendations for ecologists to select appropriate methods for sorting their specific taxonomic groups and data.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: IET Computer Vision 20(1), e70091 (2026)

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Consistency-Preserving Concept Erasure via Unsafe-Safe Pairing and Directional Fisher-Weighted Adaptation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: With the increasing versatility of text-to-image diffusion models, the ability to selectively erase undesirable concepts (e.g., harmful content) has become indispensable. However, existing concept erasure approaches primarily focus on removing unsafe concepts without providing guidance toward corresponding safe alternatives, which often leads to failure in preserving the structural and semantic consistency between the original and erased generations. In this paper, we propose a novel framework, PAIRed Erasing (PAIR), which reframes concept erasure from simple removal to consistency-preserving semantic realignment using unsafe-safe pairs. We first generate safe counterparts from unsafe inputs while preserving structural and semantic fidelity, forming paired unsafe-safe multimodal data. Leveraging these pairs, we introduce two key components: (1) Paired Semantic Realignment, a guided objective that uses unsafe-safe pairs to explicitly map target concepts to semantically aligned safe anchors; and (2) Fisher-Weighted Initialization for DoRA, which initializes parameter-efficient low-rank adaptation matrices using unsafe-safe pairs, encouraging the generation of safe alternatives while selectively suppressing unsafe concepts. Together, these components enable fine-grained erasure that removes only the targeted concepts while maintaining overall semantic consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our approach achieves the best overall trade-off among baselines, providing effective concept erasure while preserving structural integrity, semantic coherence, and generation quality.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Kelix Technical Report
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Autoregressive large language models (LLMs) scale well by expressing diverse tasks as sequences of discrete natural-language tokens and training with next-token prediction, which unifies comprehension and generation under self-supervision. Extending this paradigm to multimodal data requires a shared, discrete representation across modalities. However, most vision-language models (VLMs) still rely on a hybrid interface: discrete text tokens paired with continuous Vision Transformer (ViT) features. Because supervision is largely text-driven, these models are often biased toward understanding and cannot fully leverage large-scale self-supervised learning on non-text data. Recent work has explored discrete visual tokenization to enable fully autoregressive multimodal modeling, showing promising progress toward unified understanding and generation. Yet existing discrete vision tokens frequently lose information due to limited code capacity, resulting in noticeably weaker understanding than continuous-feature VLMs. We present Kelix, a fully discrete autoregressive unified model that closes the understanding gap between discrete and continuous visual representations.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: MamaDino: A Hybrid Vision Model for Breast Cancer 3-Year Risk Prediction
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Breast cancer screening programmes increasingly seek to move from one-size-fits-all intervals to risk-adapted and personalized strategies. Deep learning (DL) has enabled image-based risk models with stronger 1- to 5-year prediction than clinical models, but leading systems (e.g., Mirai) typically use convolutional backbones, high-resolution inputs (>1M pixels) and simple multi-view fusion, with limited explicit modelling of contralateral asymmetry. We hypothesised that combining complementary inductive biases (convolutional and transformer-based) with explicit contralateral asymmetry modelling would allow us to match state-of-the-art 3-year risk prediction performance on lower-resolution mammograms, suggesting that using less detail in a more structured way can recover state-of-the-art accuracy.
